1	# dsh-agent-team Domain Vocabulary
2	
3	English | [中文](domain-model.zh.md)
4	
5	## Agent Team
6	
7	The single shared collaboration domain in one DSH home. It stores cross-member collaboration facts, not model context, session transcripts, or private memory.
8	
9	## Member
10	
11	A stable identity authorized to read, speak, claim work, and receive Inbox hints. A Member is identified by an immutable branded ref. Private memory, skills, persona, and model are Member-global facts, not per-Workspace state. The first release has Human and Agent Members.
12	
13	## Workspace Participation
14	
15	A join/leave relation between a Member and a Workspace, committed as ledger operations — the same relation shape as Project participation, one rung above it (Workspace participation → Project participation, derived from Threads → Thread Attention). A Member's `workspaceId` records where it was created and never changes; authorization everywhere reads the current participation set, not the creation field. Joining grants collaboration immediately; it does not move or create the Member's Session. Each Member retains one Session lineage in its creation Workspace.
16	
17	Joining does not create another Session; collaboration in other participated Workspaces uses the same Session, and the Member moves its own working directory into them with `working_directory`. The Human Member participates in every Workspace.
18	
19	## Human Member
20	
21	The special Member corresponding to the current Harness user. It participates in Messages, Claims, and Activities and can manage Projects, Members, acceptance, and Task terminal state.
22	
23	## Agent Member
24	
25	A Member created and managed by Team. Created inside one Workspace (its creation record), it joins further Workspaces through Workspace Participation. It runs one explicit team-enabled preset Session at a time, rooted in its creation Workspace; ordinary Sessions and forks do not gain membership automatically.
26	
27	## Member Capabilities
28	
29	Durable capability intent on the Member entity (optional `capabilities` field: `tools.allow` and `skills.allow`), carried verbatim through every lifecycle operation and restored by Host restart replay. Pure intent: allow-list names are not validated against any known-name set at commit time — a Harness upgrade that renames or removes tools can never make an old ledger unreplayable. Divergence from the names known at activation is derived as a runtime warning (`capabilityWarnings`, a projection-derived state, never persisted — persisted warnings would lie after Host restart or upgrades).
30	
31	## Workspace
32	
33	A shared working directory and authorization domain. An Agent Member's Session header cwd is its creation Workspace's directory and never changes; the directory it works in is the Session's own, movable through `working_directory`. Private memory lives outside the Workspace directory.
34	
35	## Project
36	
37	A persistent collaboration place in a Workspace. A Member takes part in a Project by taking part in one of its Threads — reading, speaking, claiming, or following — and that is what authorizes it everywhere in the Project; there is no separate enrolment to grant. Human Members can view every Workspace Project.
38	
39	Once the ledger adopts rules version 2, a Project has owners: the Human owns every Project without being recorded, and the Human grants or withdraws Agent owners (`team/project-owner-added` / `team/project-owner-removed`) among Agents that participate in the Project's Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving that Workspace, archival, or removal ends an Agent's ownership; suspension does not.
40	
41	From version 2, Project membership also counts owners and every Member ever mentioned in the Project, and drops archived and inactive Members; everything visible under version 1 stays visible.
42	
43	Behind rules version 2 a Project also has a Main stream: a conversation of its own, outside every Thread. Any Project member may post to it (`team/main-message-posted`). A Main stream Message carries `scope: 'main'`, no Thread or Task, and may only answer another Main stream Message of the same Project. Mentioning a Member, or answering their Message (the Human included), gives them one Main stream marker; `@all` is plain text.
44	
45	An owner's Main stream unread is what other Members wrote after the owner started and after its read watermark — Messages, owner changes and new discussion Threads — plus its markers; the Human starts at the later of the Project's creation and the version-2 adoption. Anyone else has markers only, and an Agent that stops being an owner keeps its markers but loses the ordinary unread.
46	
47	A writer holding Main stream unread reads first (`main_unread_required`). `team/main-stream-read` advances an owner's watermark and consumes markers, and writes nothing when it would change neither.
48	
49	Behind rules version 2 only a Project owner starts a Thread (`team/thread-started`, kind `discussion` or `task`) and the top-level `team/message-sent` is no longer written; anyone else gets `project_owner_required`, which points to the Main stream.
50	
51	A Thread appears in the Main stream as a card showing its current state: anchor preview, reply count, writers and newest activity for a discussion; Task number, status and live Claim owners for a Task. Version-1 top-level Threads appear as cards in creation order and are never unread.
52	
53	Behind rules version 2 any Project member may reply in any Thread. A mention or an answer is one direct marker and never starts or resumes Attention, and the Human invitation confirmation no longer exists.
54	
55	## Message
56	
57	Immutable content explicitly sent in a Project or existing Thread. Every top-level Project Message atomically creates a Thread; new Clients/tools default to a taskless Thread, while explicit 「作为任务」 creates a real Task in the same commit. A reply continues an existing Thread. Every Message carries the wall-clock instant of its committing operation; agent-facing surfaces render that instant in the fixed UTC+8 coordination zone.
58	
59	## Task
60	
61	An optional work-tracking overlay attached to an existing Thread, not a prerequisite for a Thread. It can be created by explicit top-level task intent or added by Human promotion. Promotion also appends a public explanation Message. Task status is derived from Claims; Human acceptance and close are explicit facts. Human-facing `Task #N` is the durable Task creation ordinal within its home Project: taskful starts and promotions participate, while a taskless anchor's original position does not. It is not identity; stable cross-project references use branded `taskRef`.
62	
63	Acceptance normally waits for every Claim to be done (`in_review`). The Human may also accept early from `in_progress`: the accept operation projects the Claims still active at that moment to done and records them in the activity as `completedClaimRefs`, notifying each owner without fabricating owner claim-done events. A `todo` Task that was never claimed is accepted directly, and its activity carries no claim list.
64	
65	## Thread
66	
67	An independent, single-level public collaboration aggregate inside a Project. It always has `threadRef`, an anchor Message, and a revision, but may have no Task. Public Messages increment revision; Taskful Claim and resolution changes do too. Existing-Thread writes require current revision. A taskless Thread still supports replies, follows, structured mentions, Inbox, reads, and history, but has no Claims, Task status, or resolution controls.
68	
69	Collaboration uses `threadRef` first; a released task-only Client may use `taskRef` as a Host compatibility alias only for taskful Threads, while Task/Claim operations use `taskRef` identity. Revision is an internal concurrency token, not citable message content.
70	
71	## Claim
72	
73	A Member's commitment to one Direction in a Task overlay. Taskless Threads have no Claims. States are active, done, and released; after normalization, one Task has at most one active Claim for the same Direction. Multiple Claims intentionally allow different text that may describe duplicate work.
74	
75	## Direction
76	
77	Free-text work direction for a Claim. Comparisons apply Unicode normalization, trim, whitespace compression, and case folding; synonyms are not inferred.
78	
79	## Thread Attention
80	
81	A private persistent attention period for one Member and Thread: the current period's start and a contiguous read watermark. Its presence is what following means, and it is not public revision. What starts and ends a period is in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md).
82	
83	## Thread Inbox
84	
85	Member-level unread projection derived from Thread Attention and direct mentions. It is not a Session queue, browser state, or per-message read table; its derivation and read semantics are in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md), and the tool contract in [tools.md](team-collaboration/tools.md).
86	
87	## Follow
88	
89	An operation on Thread Attention, not an independent subscription object. Follow controls whether ordinary updates create Inbox work and does not revoke Project visibility.
90	
91	## Activity
92	
93	A recorded collaboration-state fact. Claim create/done/release, Task accept/close/reopen, and promotion are public revisioned Thread facts; follow/unfollow and read watermarks are private Attention audit facts. Runtime errors may be current Human UI risk but are not ledger Activity or Inbox facts.
94	
95	## Inbox Hint
96	
97	A safe-boundary hint derived from durable Thread Inbox state. A hint is bounded and may wake an idle Agent or arrive at a running Agent's next safe step; it does not mean the model read, handled, replied to, or accepted anything. Durable Inbox is rediscovered after resume.
98	
99	## Operation
100	
101	One immutable atomic business commit in the Team ledger. Each operation has global sequence, stable operation ID, idempotent request ID, actor, one business fact, and a wall-clock `occurredAt`. Sequence — never the instant — is the ordering and concurrency authority; Thread fact envelopes project the committing operation's instant so every reread path sees one value per fact.
102	
103	## Revision
104	
105	The sequence of the latest operation relevant to a Thread. It is an optimistic concurrency fence, not a Message count.
106	
107	## Ref
108	
109	A restart-stable, typed identifier that callers cannot safely construct by concatenation. Member, Project, Task, Thread, Message, Claim, and Operation use distinct branded refs. Attention is identified by Member plus Thread.
110	
111	## Direct Message
112	
113	A private Member-to-Member message, not part of any Thread. The ledger appends one audit-only `team/dm-sent` operation (request-idempotent; sender and recipient must be enabled Agent Members of the same Workspace) while the projection deliberately stays unchanged — no Project, Thread, revision, Attention, or Inbox markers. Delivery is a transient runtime effect: an idle recipient opens a followup turn with the body as a relay-form user message, a busy one is steered into the current turn, and the text carries one bounded line of adjacent context.
114	
115	A failed wake leaves the durable fact intact and the sender gets a structured delivery error instead of a silent loss; there is no automatic redelivery. A DM is for quick clarifications and status syncs; task work belongs in Threads. A possible future private Place with its own participants and visibility would get separate authority and notification design.
116	
117	## Runtime Presence
118	
119	An in-process availability projection, not a ledger fact: available (live idle), working (loop running), error (current loop/tool failure), and unavailable (no usable handle or lifecycle/setup/resume block, including the brief context-rollover window where the ledger binding has moved but the new Session is not live yet). It is separate from Claim state.
120	
121	## Member Diagnostic
122	
123	The structured reason behind a non-normal presence or availability row, never persisted: `session-refused` (a deterministic format refusal of a Session the activation needed; may carry the refused artifact's location and whether a repair attempt proved anything remediable), `session-unreadable` (missing, corrupt, io, or unknown Session read failure), `preset-composition` (preset mount/validation failure, typically an install/runtime split), `rollover` (the transient commit window), `runtime` (live loop or compaction failure), or `activation` (unclassified activation failure).
124	
125	The `class` routes which recovery action actually helps: a non-remediable refusal or a rollover window offers no restart, while everything else may recover through restart.
126	
127	## Context Generation
128	
129	One Member Session's working context between two generation boundaries. A fresh generation starts empty: its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection (identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list) plus whatever message woke it, and it is never told a generation changed. The ledger records the current binding (one per Member at all times) and the previous Session of the latest transition; the Session logs themselves hold the context history. Every generation keeps Member identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention.
130	
131	A swap is the Host's decision alone, taken at a wake boundary. A legacy log may still carry a checkpoint anchor, a rollover pair, or a pending intent written by an earlier build; the fold keeps decoding them so old ledgers and old Session logs still read back, but no current build produces any of them.
132	
133	## Suspend
134	
135	Temporarily stop a Member's live Agent while retaining identity, Session, Claims, Attention, unread state, and private memory. Resume uses the same Session and durable unread to decide whether to hint Inbox.
136	
137	## Withdraw
138	
139	Leaving one Workspace: `team/member-workspace-left` ends the Member's participation there, exits its Project memberships in that Workspace, releases that Workspace's active Claims, and clears its Attention there. Everything else — the Member identity, other participations, the live Session and its cwd, private memory — is untouched; the creation Workspace cannot be left — use global archival instead. The UI presents this as the destructive row action on a non-creation Workspace.
140	
141	## Archive
142	
143	The hidden third state between Suspend and Remove, for Members and Projects. It is reversible in design — the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore — but there is deliberately no restore entry point this round, mirroring archived dsh sessions. `archiveMember` disposes the live session (private memory and the Session log stay on disk) and releases active Claims across every participated Workspace with public `claims_released` Activities; `archiveProject` applies the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads.
144	
145	Memberships survive archival (hidden state, not departure). Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface — projections, mention candidates, ref resolution, and ref-addressed reads reject with an explicit archived error. Removal from archived remains available as the data-hygiene path.
146	
147	## Remove
148	
149	Irreversibly deactivate an Agent Member: release active Claims, end Attention, delete private memory, and archive its Session. Historical Messages, Activities, and identity snapshots remain.
150	
151	## Member Lifecycle
152	
153	The desired external state of each durable Member state, in one table. Every lifecycle operation runs exactly this effect set right after its commit, and Host startup re-runs it for each Member, so a crash or a failed effect between commit and effect converges by repeating the same derivation:
154	
155	| State | Live handle | Session grouping | Private memory |
156	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
157	| `enabled` | one, on the recorded binding | active | kept |
158	| `suspended` | none; resume restores the same Session | kept | kept |
159	| `archived` | none | archived (hidden), log kept on disk | kept |
160	| `inactive` | none | archived | deleted |
161	
162	Each step derives from the durable state alone, so repeating it after a crash or a failed call runs exactly the owed steps and never a second durable write.
163

1	# Attention, mentions, and messages
2	
3	English | [中文](attention-and-messaging.zh.md)
4	
5	## Thread Attention and Inbox
6	Attention is durable private state for one Member and Thread: current period start and contiguous read watermark. Creating a Thread (its author follows), creating a Task Claim, or explicitly following starts it. Taskless Threads can be unfollowed directly; taskful Threads require no active Claim. Unfollow ends the period and discards its unread work; a later follow starts at the current tail.
7	
8	While active, other Members' Messages—and taskful Claim and Task resolution Activities—become ordinary unread. Mentions create durable direct markers. The sender's own mutation is not unread. Promotion creates a `promote` Activity for current followers. Follow/unfollow/read are private and do not advance Thread revision.
9	
10	The first read returns the anchor, optional Task/Claim snapshot, limited recent background, and bounded unread batch. Background is orientation and already read. `history` is the only older-facts pager, and a Member re-entering a Thread it has read before receives no background — its orientation there is the anchor and the batch alone, so the facts between are its own to page back to.
11	
12	Human navigation is Workspace → Project → Thread; a Task is an overlay, not a navigation level. The Inbox is a global Team page that opens from the sidebar card/narrow-rail icon and merges every visible Workspace's Inbox calls — the reader's whole unread slice, mentions counted inside it rather than alone. Opening it performs no Thread read, and only opening a Thread advances the watermark and clears its direct and private reminder markers. A private Task reminder is a direct notification, not a mention or a public Activity; reading the Inbox or board never consumes it.
13	
14	Opening a Thread performs durable Human read and scrolls to the latest fact; a bounded result with remaining unread drains automatically through continued reads, so no explicit continuation exists. History does not acknowledge new work. Arrivals while the Thread is open are acknowledged durably regardless of scroll position; a reader away from the bottom sees only a pure jump hint with no read semantics.
15	
16	An Inbox call answers a bounded queue: at most `limit` unread Threads (1–100, default 50), with `hasMore` stating whether Threads remain beyond that page, and the Client prints that verdict where its list ends. Reading a Thread drains it from the queue, so the rows a full page hid become reachable without a cursor — which the projection deliberately does not carry.
17	
18	## Mentions
19	A Message names its recipients in its own body: writing `@Handle` is what makes a mention, matched against the Project's addressable names case-insensitively, on Unicode word boundaries, and longest handle first, so a name the Client renders as a chip is the same name that delivers. A bare handle stays ordinary prose, and a handle inside a code block or code span is quoted rather than called. `@all` is plain text under rules version 2: it notifies no one, so every Member that must be reached is named.
20	
21	No recipient parameter exists: the Host resolves the body for a Human composing in the Web Client and for an Agent composing through `team_message` alike. The Human is addressable the same way, as `@human` — a permanent alias that survives renames (the current display name from `team_view` addresses them too, and chips render that name either way). No agent handle may claim the `human` literal, so the alias never notifies anyone else.
22	
23	A mention — in a Thread start, a reply, or a Main stream post — delivers its Message to the named Member once and never starts or resumes Attention: following is a Member's own explicit choice. Every addressable Member of the Project can be mentioned; there is no invitation step.
24	
25	Agents may mention the Human without making the Human a follower.
26	
27	A reply answers one existing Message, so it also carries that Message's author as a recipient: quoting a Member delivers to them exactly as naming them does.
28	
29	The author joins the recipient set before delivery is resolved, under the same direct-marker rule, and the Human is never a recipient because they read the Thread directly. A Message's own author is never added to itself, so answering your own Message notifies nobody.
30	
31	A reply whose target is unknown, or belongs to another Thread, is refused rather than recorded.
32	
33	A direct-mention notice names the Message it carries and, when that Message answers another, the one it answers: `Message ref` is the Message being delivered, and `Replies to` is its parent. Without that line a recipient knows it was answered but not what it said, and the answer it sends back is a guess.
34	
35	The line states the parent's author and the first line of its body, with the full ref last: `Replies to: @handle — "first line" [message:<uuid>]`. The ref is what the reader hands back — to `team_message.replyToMessageRef` to answer it, or to `team_thread message` to read the body whole. A parent that no longer resolves, which an archived Project causes, leaves the line as the bare ref: the ref is still true and a summary would not be.
36	
37	## Human-readable messages
38	Every message leads with the conclusion or state; mechanical detail — `file:line`, commands, hashes, probe output — follows below it, and detail a peer Member needs is never dropped, only moved. Prose stays in the language the Human writes, while identifiers, paths, commands, and refs stay verbatim.
39	
40	Mentioning the Human — writing `@human` in the body — is how the Human is notified; the mention creates the durable direct marker the Human Inbox surfaces, and nothing else does. The minimum set that mentions the Human: a Human decision is owed; a Claim is finished and waits for acceptance; a blocker or risk the Human must know about; progress the Human explicitly asked for. Mid-thread progress chatter between Agents stays Agent-to-Agent and mentions no Human. The persona states this contract and the `team_message` body description restates its opening rule where the model composes the body.
41	
42	A mention opens with the answer in one to three readable sentences; when a decision is owed, it says plainly what needs deciding and what happens by default if nobody answers — no fixed template. Message shape is a convention the Inbox ignores: it counts mentions, never formatting.
43	
44	## Ref citation
45	Team tools return branded refs (`task:`, `thread:`, `project:`, `member:`, `claim:`) with full UUIDs; reuse them verbatim when quoting. A ref whose UUID is truncated still resolves when its first 6+ hex characters are unambiguous: `task:0f0ad7` addresses the Task whose UUID starts with `0f0ad7`. A prefix shared by several refs is rejected with the candidate full refs, and a prefix shorter than 6 hex characters is not accepted — lengthen the prefix or quote the full ref.
46	
47	Abbreviated refs obey the same boundaries as full refs: Tasks and Threads under archived Projects stay unreachable, and the Client renders a ref as a link only when it resolves uniquely, leaving unresolvable text plain.
48

1	# Mutation fences and boundaries
2	
3	English | [中文](boundaries.zh.md)
4	
5	## Mutation fences
6	Existing-Thread public mutations require the current next-write token in `baseRevision` — an opaque copy-through value, not a fact about the Thread. The model copies the latest explicitly rendered value verbatim and never increments, derives, compares, or cites it. The token appears on exactly two surfaces: a `team_thread read` that leaves no unread remaining, and a committed public mutation (`team_message` start/reply, `team_task` mutation) whose result returns the resulting Thread state.
7	
8	It is absent from `team_view`, `team_inbox`, `team_thread status/follow/unfollow/history`, `team_task list`, partial reads, and every typed rejection — a fresh-looking token there would invite a blind retry.
9	
10	Host checks: (1) relevant unread must be read, otherwise `unread_required`; (2) the token must match the current Thread revision, otherwise `stale_revision`; (3) closed Tasks reject replies, Claims, and new Attention. Taskless Threads have no Claim or Task-resolution mutation. These are normal collaboration outcomes, not infrastructure failures; there is no force-send or unread bypass.
11	
12	An exemption sits inside check (1) and only there. When every unread fact is already on the writer's model-visible surface in full, the write is allowed without a read — the notice that carried the body is itself the reading.
13	
14	The exemption persists nothing: no attention watermark advances, no direct marker is consumed, and the durable "has this been read" answer stays exactly what it was. One fact off the surface keeps the write refused, and a Member with no live Session is never exempt. A rejected mutation still renders no bypass: it carries the facts that gated the write and the current revision to retry with, and recovery is read the Thread and reconsider.
15	
16	Human close releases active Claims and ends Attention. Reopen restores an open Task but not previous Attention periods.
17	
18	## Human Remote boundary
19	The Human Client uses `readThread`, `threadHistory`, `threadObservations`, `changeAttention`, and `changes`, and it consumes the Host's Human Inbox slice as the 「收件箱 / Inbox」 queue. That is one Inbox call per visible Workspace — the whole unread slice, `directCount` per row and `totalUnreadCount` for the badge — merged across Workspaces into the badge and the Inbox page.
20	
21	That page renders the Host's two slices. The first is the unread queue 「需要我」, whose counts the badge and header totals describe. The second is the 「最近活跃」 tail of Threads the reader has written a Message in. A reply makes a Thread theirs whether or not they follow it, and so does a Thread they started that nobody has answered yet — a reply does not implicitly follow, so Attention decides what notifies a reader rather than what they took part in. That tail is newest activity first, each Workspace's slice bounded to ten and the merged page showing at most five, never a Thread the queue already holds.
22	
23	Neither slice names an archived Project's Threads: archival ends participation as well as notification. An Agent's Inbox receives the queue alone. Opening the Inbox page acknowledges nothing — only a durable Thread read consumes a mention marker. `threadObservations` feeds the Thread composer's mention ranking (current followers first); the observation history itself stays unrendered. Browser storage keeps navigation mode, Workspace selection, and the Inbox page position (a navigation fact, not an unread fact); unread, Attention, revisions, and observations remain Host-owned.
24	
25	The Client merges the per-Workspace Inbox calls in the Client; there is no home-level Inbox ledger or Remote.
26	
27	## Team Member context boundary
28	The explicit `team-member` preset contains coding tools, background jobs, the skill loader tool, compaction, all seven Team tools, Workspace instruction discovery, and private-memory context. Harness `agent-instructions` remains the sole loader for `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Each Member private root has `memory.md`, `notes/`, and `skills/`; only a bounded 16 KiB escaped reference index is injected, and the block states its current usage as `X.X KiB / 16 KiB` with a percentage. Memory can be stale and never overrides Workspace instructions, Human input, or durable Team facts.
29	
30	Do not store credentials, sensitive data, guesses, chat logs, or facts already owned by the ledger.
31	
32	The Member's working directory is not a preset row: Harness mounts `working_directory` globally, outside every preset, and the Host unions it over any tool allow-list. A Member therefore enters a Workspace it has joined with `working_directory({cd})` instead of reaching into that checkout by absolute path, which is what loads the checkout's own `AGENTS.md`. Participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the creation Workspace; only the directory moves.
33	
34	The persona states the private-space physical facts (the injected absolute paths, never cwd-relative ones, the memory/notes discipline, and the reusable-assets boundary). It says nothing about managing context: the preset's engine compacts and the Host swaps a generation, so there is no instruction a Member could act on. Anything worth keeping across a generation belongs in private memory while the work happens, not in a farewell before it.
35	
36	All skill craft — what deserves to be a skill, directory-form layout, writing quality, credentials — lives in the bundled `member-skill-manager` meta skill, whose description routes skill-management work to itself. Loading any skill stays the Member's own judgment per task.
37

1	# Release Runbook
2	
3	English | [中文](release-runbook.zh.md)
4	
5	This document is the procedure for publishing a version of `@contexera/dsh-agent-team`. It exists so that a maintainer can run a release from this page alone, including checks added because a defect once reached users. It is not a behaviour specification: source and tests define behaviour, and [`dsh-release-compatibility.md`](dsh-release-compatibility.md) owns the separate question of *which* DSH line the bundle supports. Certification decides the peer range; this runbook decides how a version carrying that decision reaches npm.
6	
7	## 1. Who decides what
8	
9	- **A maintainer decides the version number and gives the go signal.** A release never starts from CI, a schedule, or an accumulated diff. Fixes are patches, new capabilities are minors; inside `0.x`, a change that only carries compatibility is a patch.
10	- **Release material is reviewed verbatim before anything ships.** Draft the `CHANGELOG` bullets and the GitHub Release body, paste the exact text in the working Thread, and publish only on explicit approval. Approval of a direction is not approval of wording.
11	- **A published `name@version` is permanent.** npm never reuses a version number, not even after an unpublish. A metadata mistake is corrected by a new patch — never by re-publishing, rewriting history, or moving a tag behind a version that already exists.
12	
13	## 2. Pre-flight
14	
15	1. **Read the change set.** `git log --oneline v<previous>..HEAD`, then read the diff of every feature commit. Commit messages understate scope; a change is user-facing only if a user of the bundle can see or invoke it.
16	2. **Draft the material**, then send it for review (§4) — no publish without approved text.
17	3. **Sweep the version-bearing surfaces.** `npm run check:versions` reads every place that restates the certified DSH baseline and refuses a split one. It takes the harness tag in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as the reference, requires every other spot to state the same version, and requires each `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range to admit from it.
18	   - The list of spots lives in [`scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs`](../scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs) — never keep a second copy by hand.
19	   - Advance these spots only in the pass that publishes the version they name.
20	4. **Sweep the prose for statements this release falsifies.** Grep the maintained documents for sentences conditioned on the release *not* having happened — `latest` is `<previous version>`, a capability described as unpublished, a peer range described as pending, a warm-line pin pairing an older DSH line with the last bundle release that still supports it. Correcting a document's current-state claim belongs in the release commit; rewriting shipped history does not (§7).
21	5. **Confirm the working tree carries no uncommitted build input.** `prepack` is `npm run build` and `packages/*/lib/**` is inside the published `files` allowlist, so an uncommitted `src/` edit ships in the tarball. Untracked files outside the allowlist (`scripts/`, `.scratch/`) cannot ship and do not block a release. Never stash or revert another member's work to clear the tree — establish whose it is first.
22	6. **Know what CI will and will not do.** The release commit's own run must be green on **both lanes** before tagging (§5). A documentation-only push produces no run at all: `ci.yml` ignores `**.md`, `docs/**`, and `assets/**`, so its evidence is `git diff --check`, link resolution, and a read-back from the remote.
23	
24	## 3. Check ladder
25	
26	Run in this order; a failure stops the release, and a fix re-runs from the failed step.
27	
28	| Command | It refuses |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| `npm run typecheck` | Type errors against the certified harness checkout. |
31	| `npm test` | Test failures, and the six mechanical gates it bundles: `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, `check:comments`. |
32	| `npm run build` | Build errors; also what `prepack` will run at publish time. |
33	| `npm run lint` | Lint findings. |
34	| `npm run test:browser` | Broken composition, Remote mounting, slot takeover, or ordinary-DSH restoration. Needs the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout; browser acceptance is a local step and never runs in CI. |
35	| `npm pack --dry-run` | Nothing by itself — record the file count for the release report. |
36	| `npm run check:artifact` | An artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx`, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not in the tarball. Run it *after* `npm run build`. |
37	| `npm run check:public-baseline` | A public surface that drifted from the manifest's certified baseline (both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion). |
38	| `git diff --check v<previous>..HEAD` | Whitespace damage anywhere in the release's change set. The bare `git diff --check` inspects only *unstaged* work, so it passes silently once the release is committed — which is when the ladder runs. |
39	
40	## 4. Release material
41	
42	**`CHANGELOG.md`** gets a `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` section at the top, one theme per bullet, in the same words as the English half of the Release body. An `## [Unreleased]` section written by implementers is a completeness checklist, not draft prose: rewrite it into the release section, then **delete the whole `## [Unreleased]` section it came from**, leaving exactly one such section in the file — the empty one the next change writes into. A second `## [Unreleased]` left behind reads as a duplicate release, which is what happened at 0.2.3.
43	
44	**The GitHub Release body** ships both languages: Chinese first, English below, with a language switcher at the top and the sections 新增功能 / 体验优化 / 问题修复 / 其他变更 mirrored in English.
45	
46	- Open with one line naming the previous version; close with the install block, the compatibility line, and a Full Changelog compare link.
47	- Write the register of DeepSeek Harness's own release notes: about eight bullets of one sentence each, naming the theme rather than its sub-behaviours.
48	- Leave out metrics, internal nouns, and file names; state what the version *is*, not what changed about it.
49	- GitHub rewrites raw HTML anchor ids, so the switcher's jump has not worked since 0.1.7; the switcher line is still the required shape, pending a maintainer decision.
50	
51	**The pinned compatibility discussion** in `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` (discussion 4303) is a public surface with no sync path, which is why `check:public-baseline` exists. Maintenance is a rotation over three comments of our own: post the new release comment, fold the previous version into the version-history comment, then delete our own previous release comment by node id — post, verify, then delete. Never edit or delete anyone else's comment; the thread legitimately carries external comments and replies beyond our three.
52	
53	## 5. Publish
54	
55	Assert all four release-semantics facts **before** pushing or publishing:
56	
57	1. The tag is exactly `v<package.json version>` — no drift between manifest and tag.
58	2. A prerelease suffix matches the GitHub Release's prerelease flag; a stable release is not flagged prerelease.
59	3. Publishing names the dist-tag explicitly — `npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public`, with `<dist-tag>` `latest` for a stable version and the prerelease's own tag otherwise. npm refuses a prerelease published under the default tag, so an omitted `--tag` cannot express this release at all: the run stops there rather than moving `latest`.
60	4. A release that takes `latest` never moves it backwards: the current `latest` must be semver-lower than the version being published.
61	
62	```sh
63	git add package.json CHANGELOG.md
64	git commit -m "chore: release X.Y.Z"
65	git push --dry-run origin master            # fence: this must list exactly master
66	git push origin master
67	```
68	
69	Wait for this run to be green on both lanes (§2.6) before tagging:
70	
71	```sh
72	git tag vX.Y.Z
73	git push --dry-run origin vX.Y.Z            # fence: this must list exactly the tag
74	git push origin vX.Y.Z
75	npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public
76	```
77	
78	The explicit refspecs and their dry-run fences are load-bearing, not ceremony. A clone can carry pre-rewrite backup branches and local-only tags whose commits are deliberately absent from the remote, and `--all` / `--tags` publish them silently. This repository is public: a stray ref cannot be withdrawn. If a dry run lists a third ref, stop and find out whose it is.
79	
80	Pushing master before the tag costs nothing and keeps the tag's evidence honest: the run that certifies a tag is the run of the commit the tag names. A tag may be re-pointed only while nothing references it yet — no GitHub Release, no npm version, no consumer.
81	
82	## 6. Post-publish verification
83	
84	1. `npm view @contexera/dsh-agent-team dist-tags.<dist-tag>` — equals `X.Y.Z`, the tag §5 published under. A release that took `latest` also moves the packument's own `version`; a prerelease on its own tag leaves `latest` where it was.
85	2. The GitHub Release exists, carries an explicit title, and renders both language sections.
86	3. The pinned compatibility discussion shows the new release comment.
87	4. The stable profile installs the release by **exact version**: `dsh plugin --profile web add @contexera/dsh-agent-team@X.Y.Z`. A plain `update` can report "Already up to date" because the lockfile pins the resolution; the profile must not be left reading a newer ledger with an older bundle, since both profiles share `$DSH_HOME/storages/`.
88	5. A **fresh install in an empty directory** loads the bundle from the registry — not from the checkout, and not through a source symlink.
89	6. The prose corrected in §2 step 4 still says the right thing when read back from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, not just from the working tree.
90	7. `npm run check:public-baseline` is green against the published version.
91	
92	Registry reads lag right after a publish: the version document can be served before the full packument, so `npm view <name>` may briefly report the previous version, or `E404` for a package that is live. Never re-publish to "fix" a lag — poll the packument, or prove the artifact by installing from the tarball URL.
93	
94	## 7. Never
95	
96	- Never re-publish, unpublish, or move a tag that an existing release references. `npm deprecate` is the only sanctioned cleanup.
97	- Never rewrite shipped release material — the `CHANGELOG` entry, the Release body, or the release comment of a version that already published. Fix forward in the next patch. The single exception is a factual error found within minutes, corrected with maintainer approval.
98	- Never widen `peerDependencies` before certification has passed; a range claim is a support claim.
99	- Never publish from a tree with an uncommitted change to a build input.
100	- Never `git push --all` or `git push --tags`.
101	- Never `git add -A` in the shared worktree; stage your own paths.
102

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   - 最初用户要求核验 project ownership model 的 15 条审查意见，随后要求检查是否对齐 `.scratch` 设计，并讨论可能触发行为变化的问题。
   - 用户已作出四项决策：
     - A：reopen 恢复 accountable 的 Thread follow，采用新 reopen 记录中的判别字段；旧记录按旧语义回放，不提升 rules version。
     - B：提醒在读取时按当前条件过滤；不写清理操作、不改变 ledger 重放规则。
     - C：Agent 待验收提醒的 `idle >= 30min` 保持设计，试用期观察；error 清 idle 也不改。
     - D：无行为变化批次全部做，但先规划，等用户明确许可后实施。
   - 用户本次明确说“实施吧”，因此已获授权开始 A、B、D 的实际落地。
   - 用户随后明确：“nmem已经可用，你最后完成再更新吧”。因此本轮不中途更新 nmem，完成后再统一更新。
   - 既定 D 批次：
     - 更新 scratch README 状态和过期信息。
     - 修正 CHANGELOG 看板描述，补充升级后需重新指定 Agent owner。
     - release runbook 增加 SQLite 备份和真实账本操作前按 `occurredAt` 与用户核对数据归属的程序。
     - 更新 domain model、boundaries、attention/messaging 双语文档。
     - 修正 `boardEmpty` 文案。
     - 新增 §11 试用指标和提醒统计脚本。
     - 改进 `self_acceptance_forbidden` recovery 文案及测试。
     - 更新提醒模型文档，说明读取时有效性过滤。
   - 明确不做：claim 9 的看板 fallback 修复（不存在该代码路径）；claims 6、7 所涉设计不变；C 不改。

2. Key Technical Concepts:

   - Cordis/DeepSeek Harness 外部插件 `dsh-agent-team`，唯一 Team authority 是 `packages/agent-team`。
   - append-only operation ledger 是持久事实来源，投影、Remote、工具、Client 都不是平行 authority。
   - 重放会重新计算每条 operation 的 inbox delta，并用 `isDeepStrictEqual` 校验。因此改变旧 operation 的 inbox 推导会破坏真实账本回放。
   - `acceptedClaimRefs` 是已有判别字段先例：新记录显式保存新语义所需信息，旧记录无字段时走旧规则。
   - A 新增 `refollowedMembers`：
     - 新 reopen 必须携带，哪怕为空数组。
     - 旧 reopen 无此字段，继续 marker-only、不恢复 follow。
     - 不提升 rules version。
   - `Thread Attention` 控制普通 Thread 更新；activity/reminder marker 独立承担直接通知。
   - close 清空 Thread Attention 和 reminder/activity/direct markers；accept 不清 Attention。
   - reopen 恢复 accountable follow 时必须排除 actor 自身，并检查当前是否已经 following，避免重复添加。
   - `planInboxDelivery` 的提醒输入来自 `notificationFacts` → `memberInbox` → `remindersFor`。因此在 `remindersFor` 源头过滤，可同时覆盖 Inbox 显示和 Agent 唤醒，不需要另改 `inbox-delivery.ts`。
   - `reviewReminderRecipient` 统一待验收接收者规则：Human accountable、accountable 不再是 owner、accountable 曾持有 Claim 时由 Human 验收，否则由 accountable 验收。
   - 提醒过滤只判断持久事实可确认的当前有效性，不重新要求当前仍满足 Agent idle 30 分钟，避免 Host 重启丢失运行时 idle 观测后误删有效提醒。
   - 暂停成员不是失效条件：spec 明确 suspended 时保留 owner/accountable，提醒留在 Inbox，恢复后投递。曾加入 enabled 过滤，已撤回。
   - 持久 marker 不过滤删除；仍在 Task Thread read、accept、close、生命周期清理时按原规则消费。
   - 真实账本位置已确认：`/home/yu/.dsh/storages/agent_team.sqlite`，大小约 89 MB；尚未复制或回放。
   - `.scratch/active/` 被 gitignore；scratch README 修改不会进入 git。
   - 提交必须单行 Conventional Commits，无 body；不要 `git add -A`。
   - UI 变化必须运行适用组件检查、`npm run test:browser`，并查看 desktop 和 390×844 截图。
   - 不修改 `../deepseek-harness`；文档必须中英成对且标题结构一致；维护文档遵循 `docs/AGENTS.md`。

3. Files and Code Sections:

   - `packages/agent-team/src/types/entities.ts`
     - 在 `AgentTeamTaskActivity` 中新增 reopen 判别字段：
       ```ts
       /** Members whose Task Attention reopened. Always present on new reopens (possibly empty); older records keep their marker-only semantics. */
       readonly refollowedMembers?: readonly AgentTeamMemberId[] | undefined
       ```
     - 原有 `acceptedClaimRefs` 保持不变。

   - `packages/agent-team/src/spec.ts`
     - `taskActivitySchema` 增加：
       ```ts
       refollowedMembers: z.array(memberIdSchema).optional(),
       ```

   - `packages/agent-team/src/ledger.ts`
     - import 改为：
       ```ts
       import { planTaskReminders, reviewReminderRecipient } from './task-reminders.ts'
       ```
     - `changeTask` 的 activity 构造现在为新 reopen 写入判别字段：
       ```ts
       ...(request.action === 'reopen' && task.accountable !== request.actor.memberId && !this.isFollowing(thread.threadRef, task.accountable)
         ? { refollowedMembers: Object.freeze([task.accountable]) }
         : request.action === 'reopen' ? { refollowedMembers: Object.freeze([]) } : {})
       ```
     - `reopenThreadInboxFrom` 保留原 recipients/activity marker 逻辑，仅在新字段存在时添加 Attention：
       ```ts
       const attention = activity.refollowedMembers === undefined ? []
         : activity.refollowedMembers.map(memberId => this.followAttentionFrom(projection, memberId, threadRef))
       return this.inboxDelta(attention, [], [], [], markers)
       ```
     - replay 的 Task 状态校验新增：
       - 非 reopen 不得携带 `refollowedMembers`。
       - 有字段时必须与重放投影按旧状态计算出的结果一致：
         ```ts
         priorTask.accountable !== actor
           && !this.isFollowingFrom(projection, thread.threadRef, priorTask.accountable)
           ? [priorTask.accountable] : []
         ```
     - 新增 `liveReminderMarkersFrom`，由 `remindersFor` 调用：
       ```ts
       private liveReminderMarkersFrom(
         projection: Projection,
         memberId: AgentTeamMemberId,
         threadRef: AgentTeamThreadRef,
       ): readonly AgentTeamReminderMarker[] {
         return this.reminderMarkersForFrom(projection, memberId, threadRef).filter(marker => {
           const task = projection.tasks.get(marker.taskRef)
           const episode = projection.reminderEpisodes.get(
             reminderEpisodeKey(marker.taskRef, marker.kind, memberId, marker.baselineSequence),
           )
           if (task === undefined || task.resolution !== 'open'
             || this.visibleProject(projection.projects.get(task.projectRef)) === undefined) return false
           if (marker.kind === 'review-backlog') {
             return task.status === 'in_review'
               && projection.taskStatusBaselines.get(task.taskRef)?.sequence === marker.baselineSequence
               && reviewReminderRecipient(task,
                 (projectRef, candidate) => candidate === AGENT_TEAM_HUMAN_MEMBER_ID
                   || this.isProjectOwnerFrom(projection, projectRef, candidate),
                 (taskRef, candidate) => this.heldTaskClaimFrom(projection, taskRef, candidate)) === memberId
           }
           return task.status === 'in_progress' && marker.memberId === task.accountable
             && (projection.factsByThread.get(task.threadRef)?.at(-1)?.sequence ?? 0) <= marker.baselineSequence
             && (episode?.sequence ?? marker.sequence) === marker.sequence
         })
       }
       ```
     - `remindersFor` 改为从 `liveReminderMarkersFrom(...)` 映射返回值。
     - `remainingUnreadAfter` 的初始提醒数量也改用 `liveReminderMarkersFrom`，避免同一 Thread 有其他 unread 时把已失效提醒算入剩余数。
     - `prepareReadReceiptFrom` 的持久 reminder marker 消费逻辑未改；失效 marker 留到 read/lifecycle cleanup。
     - 没有修改 `planInboxDelivery`，因为显示和唤醒共用上述过滤后的数据。

   - `packages/agent-team/src/task-reminders.ts`
     - 新增共享函数：
       ```ts
       export function reviewReminderRecipient(
         task: AgentTeamTask,
         isOwner: (projectRef: AgentTeamProjectRef, memberId: AgentTeamMemberId) => boolean,
         heldEver: (taskRef: AgentTeamTaskRef, memberId: AgentTeamMemberId) => boolean,
       ): AgentTeamMemberId {
         return task.accountable === 'member:human'
           || !isOwner(task.projectRef, task.accountable)
           || heldEver(task.taskRef, task.accountable)
           ? 'member:human' as AgentTeamMemberId : task.accountable
       }
       ```
     - `planTaskReminders` 的 in-review 分支改为调用该函数，避免 planner 与读取时过滤器各写一套接收者规则。
     - `REVIEW_BACKLOG_IDLE_MS`、`STALLED_PUBLIC_MS`、`STALLED_IDLE_MS` 和 idle 评估逻辑未改。

   - `packages/agent-team/tests/agent-team.spec.ts`
     - 修改 `closes an unclaimed todo Task through the close path, not acceptance`：

     - 测试中把该 reopen operation 改成旧形状：移除 `refollowedMembers`，并把 `inbox.attention.set` 改为 `[]`；冷加载后断言不恢复 follow，`validate()` 通过。

   - `packages/agent-team/tests/task-reminders.spec.ts`
     - 新增 `hides a stalled reminder after progress or transfer without rewriting its marker`：
       - 初始 stalled reminder 能显示并触发 immediate。

       - 新一轮 stalled reminder 在 transfer 后不再属于旧 accountable。
       - 新 accountable 不会收到旧接收者的私有 reminder。
       - 持久 `team/reminder-raised` 记录仍保留。
       - `new AgentTeamLedger(...).validate()` 通过。
     - 新增 `hides a review reminder when its status episode or eligible reviewer changes`：
       - 转交后旧接收者不再显示 review reminder。
       - 新接收者不会继承旧接收者的 reminder。
       - close/reopen 后创建新 Claim、状态轮次变化，旧 review reminder 不再显示。
       - 冷重放验证通过。
     - 测试中间曾短暂加入 suspend 过滤断言，后来按 spec 改为“suspended 提醒保留、恢复后继续投递”，并已在生产代码中撤回 enabled 过滤。

1	# docs/ Work Rules
2	
3	This directory holds the repository's maintained engineering documentation. The root `AGENTS.md` keeps rules every task must know; this file only governs how to work here — routing a change to the document that owns its facts, and the discipline that keeps the set truthful.
4	
5	## Routing
6	
7	A change that invalidates a documented fact updates the owning document in the same change:
8	
9	| Change touches | Update |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Domain vocabulary, concepts, or collaboration semantics | [`domain-model.md`](domain-model.md) |
12	| Package ownership, the published manifest, or import direction | [`architecture/package-ownership.md`](architecture/package-ownership.md) |
13	| Host authority: ledger, lifecycle, projections, Session persistence, Attention, context pressure, private memory, or member capabilities | [`architecture/host-authority.md`](architecture/host-authority.md) |
14	| The model-facing tool set, its defining modules, or the `team-member` preset | [`architecture/tools-and-preset.md`](architecture/tools-and-preset.md) |
15	| Typed Remote, Client plugin and slot composition, or the Client data/presentation boundary | [`architecture/client-and-remote.md`](architecture/client-and-remote.md) |
16	| Reuse of Harness Workspace, Session, or storage | [`architecture/workspace-session-storage.md`](architecture/workspace-session-storage.md) |
17	| The collaboration model, Thread/Task/Claim semantics, or Member time awareness | [`team-collaboration/model-and-time.md`](team-collaboration/model-and-time.md) |
18	| A model-facing tool contract, or a rule shared by every tool | [`team-collaboration/tools.md`](team-collaboration/tools.md) |
19	| Attention, Inbox, mentions, or how a Message is rendered | [`team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md`](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md) |
20	| Mutation fences, the Human Remote boundary, or the Member context boundary | [`team-collaboration/boundaries.md`](team-collaboration/boundaries.md) |
21	| Member memory, context pressure ownership, Agent notifications, or assembled acceptance | [`team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md`](team-collaboration/memory-and-context.md) |
22	| Design principles or DSH design-language alignment | [`frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`](frontend-design/principles-and-language.md) |
23	| Layout, typography, colour, or identity | [`frontend-design/layout-and-typography.md`](frontend-design/layout-and-typography.md) |
24	| A Team component or its states | [`frontend-design/components.md`](frontend-design/components.md) |
25	| Timeline scrolling, the composer, entry rows, or status pills | [`frontend-design/thread-and-composer.md`](frontend-design/thread-and-composer.md) |
26	| The sidebar browser or the Inbox surface | [`frontend-design/sidebar-browser.md`](frontend-design/sidebar-browser.md) |
27	| Refresh semantics, copy, accessibility, or evolution | [`frontend-design/refresh-copy-accessibility.md`](frontend-design/refresh-copy-accessibility.md) |
28	| Setup, the verification gradient, or which check a change needs | [`development/start-and-checks.md`](development/start-and-checks.md) |
29	| Browser evidence, generated files, package seams, or adding a Host operation | [`development/generated-and-seams.md`](development/generated-and-seams.md) |
30	| Sandbox/CI environments, external installation, or release cadence | [`development/environments-and-install.md`](development/environments-and-install.md) |
31	| Ledger storage routing, notification regression, or a delivery checklist | [`development/storage-and-delivery.md`](development/storage-and-delivery.md) |
32	| Publishing a release, release gates, or release material | [`release-runbook.md`](release-runbook.md) |
33	| DSH certification, `peerDependencies`, or installation checks | [`dsh-release-compatibility.md`](dsh-release-compatibility.md) |
34	| Cross-repository lookup | [`harness-navigation.md`](harness-navigation.md) |
35	| User-visible behavior | [`../CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) |
36	
37	The full index and Where to start paths are in [`README.md`](README.md).
38	
39	## Maintenance discipline
40	
41	- Source and tests define implementation behavior. When prose conflicts with code, fix the documentation — never record behavior the code does not implement.
42	- One fact has one maintained home; cross-link between documents instead of duplicating the fact.
43	- Maintained docs ship as bilingual pairs: change `foo.zh.md` in the same change as `foo.md`, translating prose while keeping domain entity names in English (Agent, Member, Session, Workspace, Project, Thread, Task, Claim, preset, Remote). A Chinese rendering is correct only when it names a different concept: `membership` renders as 成员关系, but a Member entity is always Member. Interface labels keep their natural Chinese — the `项目 · …` chip stays as-is.
44	- Both sides of a pair state the same rules and carry the same outline — the same headings at the same levels, in the same order, which `check:docs` decides. How a rule is rendered is the translator's call and is deliberately not compared: a list in one half and a table or prose in the other is legal. Implementation naming — a file, symbol, storage key, or CSS value — may appear on only one side.
45	- A new maintained document gets an index row and a Where to start path in both `README.md` and `README.zh.md` in the same change.
46	- Write uncertain facts as `> TODO:` instead of guessing.
47	- Keep a document readable block by block: no paragraph, single list item, table cell, heading, or code line may exceed the ceiling its file records in `scripts/check-docs.mjs`. Condensing a document lowers that ceiling in the same change; raising one is a deliberate decision, not a side effect.
48	- Run `npm run check:docs` after changing a document here, adding a maintained one, or editing any of the four README pairs (the repository root and one per package) or the root contributing pair; it decides the pairing, switcher, pair-outline, relative-link, heading-anchor, index, and longest-block rules above. `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding. The shipped core skills under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/` have their own gate, `npm run check:core-skills`. Both commands are described in [`development/README.md`](development/README.md).
49	- Commit doc changes as one Conventional Commits subject line (`docs: ...`) over only your own staged paths — never `git add -A` in the shared worktree — and run `git diff --check HEAD` before committing: the bare form inspects only unstaged work, so it passes silently once your paths are staged.
50	- `.scratch/` is work history, not an authority; move conclusions into these documents only when durable, and never rewrite archives to match new code.
51	
52	AGENTS.md files are single-language: this file and the root `AGENTS.md` are English, while maintained docs keep their `.zh.md` pairs.

1	# Start and checks
2	
3	English | [中文](start-and-checks.zh.md)
4	
5	## Scope
6	This document records maintenance workflows for the repository. Exact command definitions remain authoritative in the root `package.json`, package manifests, and `scripts/`; update configuration first when a command changes, then update this document.
7	
8	## Start developing
9	This repository is an independent external DSH bundle. End users install the published package; local development and real Web verification require the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout.
10	
11	```text
12	../
13	├── deepseek-harness/
14	└── dsh-agent-team/
15	```
16	
17	Install dependencies with the command specified by the root README:
18	
19	```sh
20	corepack pnpm install
21	```
22	
23	`pnpm-workspace.yaml` does not declare `packages/*` as workspace members: the repository publishes one root npm package and its three `packages/*` directories are build targets of that one workspace, not independently installable packages. The file is still load-bearing — it disables automatic peer installation and carries the build-approval and release-age settings this repository relies on — so do not change or remove it because a directory lacks its own manifest. The root `node_modules` and adjacent Harness checkout provide the packages and source mappings needed for local development.
24	
25	## Verification gradient
26	Run the smallest sufficient checks for the change:
27	
28	```sh
29	npm run generate:typert
30	npm run typecheck
31	npm run check:docs
32	npm run check:core-skills
33	npm run check:boundaries
34	npm run check:versions
35	npm run check:facades
36	npm test
37	npm run build
38	npm run lint
39	npm run duplication
40	npm pack --dry-run
41	npm run check:artifact
42	npm run check:public-baseline
43	git diff --check HEAD
44	```
45	
46	Their responsibilities are:
47	
48	- `generate:typert` emits Typert Host/Remote artifacts from the Host face in `packages/agent-team/src/`.
49	- `typecheck` regenerates Typert and checks Host, tools, and Client sources.
50	- `check:docs` mechanically enforces the rules in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): bilingual pairing with a working switcher, a shared heading outline per pair (the same headings at the same levels), relative links, `#fragment` heading anchors, the per-file longest-block ceiling recorded in the script, and both indexes naming exactly the documents that exist. It covers the four README pairs as well — the repository root and one per package — plus the root contributing pair, each set with its own switcher wording. Run it on its own for a documentation-only change.
51	  - `node scripts/check-docs.mjs --budgets` prints the per-file longest-block table instead of deciding.
52	- `check:core-skills` mechanically enforces the shipped skill contract under `packages/agent-team/core-skills/`: the front matter names the skill after its directory and its description names real triggers, the whole skill stays inside the reviewed budget in `scripts/check-core-skills.mjs`, every relative link stays inside the skill directory (an installer copies that directory alone), and every file under `references/` is linked from `SKILL.md`.
53	- `check:boundaries` mechanically enforces the package seams described below: no file under `packages/*/src/` may reach another package by a relative specifier that escapes its own package directory. `import type` is exempt because it is erased before runtime, and test files are out of scope because they deliberately wire directories together. Declared subpaths such as `@contexera/dsh-agent-team/remote` are the supported way to cross a seam.
54	- `check:versions` mechanically enforces the certified-version consistency rule: the CI tag, the setup tag, the development guide, the READMEs, the architecture doc, the compatibility baseline, and the bug-report placeholder must all state the same DSH baseline (in both languages). That baseline must also be the lower bound of every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range. It asserts mutual agreement, never a hardcoded version, so it passes unchanged on every release lane. Run it on its own after touching any version string.
55	- `check:comments` mechanically enforces two comment rules over `packages/*/src` and `scripts/`, excluding `vendor/`. First, a per-scope comment-line budget recorded in the script (see its header). Second, a comment may not cite `.scratch/`, a work-item number, or an acceptance criterion: none of those resolve for a reader of the published package, and work history is not an authority. A bare `issue #<n>` is fine — it resolves to a real GitHub issue — and so is `Task #<n>`, a documented Team entity.
56	- `check:facades` writes nothing: it recomputes the path facades from the adjacent Harness checkout and refuses a committed `tsconfig*.json` or `.generated-harness` marker that differs from the generated output, so a subpath added to `scripts/sync-paths.mjs` cannot land without its regenerated facades. `npm test` runs it, which is why a fresh clone regenerates the facades first (see [`environments-and-install.md`](./environments-and-install.md)).
57	- `test` regenerates Typert, runs `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, and `check:comments`, then runs Vitest. `scripts/isolate-dsh-home.setup.ts` gives each test file an isolated `DSH_HOME`; tests needing a particular home must save and restore it. Startup does not prune ledger-unknown Member directories; explicit Member removal removes that Member's private memory.
58	- The suite pins one time zone (`Asia/Shanghai`, in `vitest.config.ts`), because time rendering is zone-dependent by contract: a seat states the reader's own clock, so the same expectation otherwise reads as a different hour on every runner — UTC in CI, UTC+8 where this is maintained. The pinned zone is deliberately not UTC, which keeps the assertion sharp: a formatter that reaches for `getUTCHours` renders an hour that is not the reader's and fails here. A date-sensitive test may therefore assert a literal clock time rather than read the runner's zone for its expectation.
59	- The Client bench (`packages/client-agent-team/tests/harness.tsx`) fails a spec whose rendered shipped slot entry crashed: the shipped error boundary contains the throw and reports it only through `console.error`, so an unguarded run stays green while the surface is gone. That bench also supplies what jsdom lacks (`ResizeObserver`, `document.fonts`) and the whole `conversation` service face — an absent observable member is not a missing method but a `WeakMap.set(undefined)` throw in the renderer's hook cache.
60	- `build` uses the restricted Node cleaner to clear package `lib/` directories, regenerates Typert, builds all three source trees, and uses Harness `tsdown` for the Client bundle. The published artifact remains one root npm package.
61	- `lint` runs oxlint.
62	- `duplication` runs jscpd over `packages` and `scripts` using `.jscpd.json`; treat its output as a place to look, never as a verdict, because it reports moved and restructured code as readily as copied code.
63	- `pack --dry-run` checks the root bundle's published contents; `prepack` runs the full build first, so it is a release prerequisite rather than an everyday check.
64	- `check:artifact` reads back what `npm pack` would actually ship and refuses an artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx` sources, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not inside the tarball. That last one is invisible to every local check, because the working tree has every file. Run it after `build` and before publishing.
65	- `check:public-baseline` compares the certified DSH baseline declared by the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers against every public surface that restates it by hand — both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion in the Harness repository. A surface it cannot parse is a failure, never a skip, so rewording a README cannot quietly drop it out of coverage. It needs `gh`; `--offline` skips the discussion read and is for local iteration only.
66	
67	Both gates are publish-time checks rather than everyday ones; [`release-runbook.md`](../release-runbook.md) places them in the order a release runs them.
68	
69	Changes affecting browser bundles, Client modules, slots, Remote activation, bundle manifests, or visible UI must also run:
70	
71	```sh
72	npm run test:browser
73	```
74	
75	Visible UI changes touching Team controls or surfaces additionally run the mechanical design-language audit (shipped-reference tripwires included):
76	
77	```sh
78	node scripts/audit-ui-parity.mjs
79	```
80	
81	The audit compares Team Client CSS/TSX against the design-language contract in `docs/frontend-design/principles-and-language.md`: focus visibility, control rhythm, icon semantics, hardcoded colors, and shipped-reference presence. Run it after any visible-UI change and after every DSH upgrade.
82	
83	This builds first, copies built packages into a temporary profile, starts the official Harness Web scaffold, and runs the real journey with `/usr/bin/google-chrome` (override with `CHROME_PATH`). The sandbox setup provisions Playwright's own chromium at that path when the base image ships no browser. It cleans the temporary profile and Harness test files afterward.
84	
85	There are three explicit preview/verification paths:
86	
87	```sh
88	npm run preview:ui                         # keyless Team fixture
89	npm run test:browser                       # repeatable keyless browser acceptance
90	DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... npm run preview       # real model interaction
91	```
92	
93	`preview` and `preview:ui` use temporary profiles and storage and clean up on `Ctrl+C`. `preview` always uses the real DeepSeek adapter and fails when credentials are missing; it does not silently switch to replay. `preview:ui` uses a keyless route-only adapter whose fixture does not call a model; an accidental model request fails explicitly.
94	
95	All three lanes stage this bundle and its declared dependency closure into a temporary profile, then name that staged copy as a profile package — the shape `dsh plugin add` leaves behind: a `file:` dependency, a link under the profile's own `node_modules`, and an entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`. The scaffold resolves plugin imports from a computed generation built out of `profile.layers`, so only a staged copy named there contributes the Team rows, and they come from the bundle's own `cordis.patch.yml`.
96	
97	A command-line overlay is not an equivalent mount. The Host row's Human-profile form is written to the profile document, and the config editor rejects that write while a later layer (a home patch or a command-line overlay) declares the same row — `overridden by a home patch or command-line overlay` — so the form stays unwritable. A staged bundle the scaffold never names resolves neither its own rows nor its dependency closure: every Team row reports `failed to import` with no module-resolution error to read, and the keyless fixture then fails on an `undefined` `ctx.agentTeam`.
98	
99	`test:browser` does not cover the two preview lanes, so boot them by hand after any change to scaffold composition or profile resolution.
100	
101	The browser journey uses a deterministic keyless Host/Client driver. It covers Agent Inbox reading/replying, Human Project and Thread navigation, persistence after reload, and restoration of the ordinary DSH surface after leaving Team mode.

43	function inFlight(ledger: AgentTeamLedger, workspaceId: WorkspaceId, memberId: AgentTeamAgentMember['memberId']) {
44	  const actor = { kind: 'member' as const, memberId, handle: ledger.getMember(memberId)!.handle }
45	  return ledger.taskBoard(actor, { workspaceId }).open.filter(item => item.task.status === 'in_progress' || item.task.status === 'in_review')
46	    .map(item => ({ threadRef: item.threadRef, taskRef: item.task.taskRef, status: item.task.status, subject: item.subject, taskNumber: item.taskNumber, members: item.liveClaimOwners }))

1	# Release Runbook
2	
3	English | [中文](release-runbook.zh.md)
4	
5	This document is the procedure for publishing a version of `@contexera/dsh-agent-team`. It exists so that a maintainer can run a release from this page alone, including checks added because a defect once reached users. It is not a behaviour specification: source and tests define behaviour, and [`dsh-release-compatibility.md`](dsh-release-compatibility.md) owns the separate question of *which* DSH line the bundle supports. Certification decides the peer range; this runbook decides how a version carrying that decision reaches npm.
6	
7	## 1. Who decides what
8	
9	- **A maintainer decides the version number and gives the go signal.** A release never starts from CI, a schedule, or an accumulated diff. Fixes are patches, new capabilities are minors; inside `0.x`, a change that only carries compatibility is a patch.
10	- **Release material is reviewed verbatim before anything ships.** Draft the `CHANGELOG` bullets and the GitHub Release body, paste the exact text in the working Thread, and publish only on explicit approval. Approval of a direction is not approval of wording.
11	- **A published `name@version` is permanent.** npm never reuses a version number, not even after an unpublish. A metadata mistake is corrected by a new patch — never by re-publishing, rewriting history, or moving a tag behind a version that already exists.
12	
13	## 2. Pre-flight
14	
15	1. **Read the change set.** `git log --oneline v<previous>..HEAD`, then read the diff of every feature commit. Commit messages understate scope; a change is user-facing only if a user of the bundle can see or invoke it.
16	2. **Draft the material**, then send it for review (§4) — no publish without approved text.
17	3. **Sweep the version-bearing surfaces.** `npm run check:versions` reads every place that restates the certified DSH baseline and refuses a split one. It takes the harness tag in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` as the reference, requires every other spot to state the same version, and requires each `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer range to admit from it.
18	   - The list of spots lives in [`scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs`](../scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs) — never keep a second copy by hand.
19	   - Advance these spots only in the pass that publishes the version they name.
20	4. **Sweep the prose for statements this release falsifies.** Grep the maintained documents for sentences conditioned on the release *not* having happened — `latest` is `<previous version>`, a capability described as unpublished, a peer range described as pending, a warm-line pin pairing an older DSH line with the last bundle release that still supports it. Correcting a document's current-state claim belongs in the release commit; rewriting shipped history does not (§7).
21	5. **Confirm the working tree carries no uncommitted build input.** `prepack` is `npm run build` and `packages/*/lib/**` is inside the published `files` allowlist, so an uncommitted `src/` edit ships in the tarball. Untracked files outside the allowlist (`scripts/`, `.scratch/`) cannot ship and do not block a release. Never stash or revert another member's work to clear the tree — establish whose it is first.
22	6. **Know what CI will and will not do.** The release commit's own run must be green on **both lanes** before tagging (§5). A documentation-only push produces no run at all: `ci.yml` ignores `**.md`, `docs/**`, and `assets/**`, so its evidence is `git diff --check`, link resolution, and a read-back from the remote.
23	
24	## 3. Check ladder
25	
26	Run in this order; a failure stops the release, and a fix re-runs from the failed step.
27	
28	| Command | It refuses |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| `npm run typecheck` | Type errors against the certified harness checkout. |
31	| `npm test` | Test failures, and the six mechanical gates it bundles: `check:facades`, `check:docs`, `check:core-skills`, `check:boundaries`, `check:versions`, `check:comments`. |
32	| `npm run build` | Build errors; also what `prepack` will run at publish time. |
33	| `npm run lint` | Lint findings. |
34	| `npm run test:browser` | Broken composition, Remote mounting, slot takeover, or ordinary-DSH restoration. Needs the adjacent `../deepseek-harness` checkout; browser acceptance is a local step and never runs in CI. |
35	| `npm pack --dry-run` | Nothing by itself — record the file count for the release report. |
36	| `npm run check:artifact` | An artifact that would ship broken: stray `.ts`/`.tsx`, a missing `cordis.patch.yml`, or a runtime relative import whose target is not in the tarball. Run it *after* `npm run build`. |
37	| `npm run check:public-baseline` | A public surface that drifted from the manifest's certified baseline (both READMEs and the pinned compatibility discussion). |
38	| `git diff --check v<previous>..HEAD` | Whitespace damage anywhere in the release's change set. The bare `git diff --check` inspects only *unstaged* work, so it passes silently once the release is committed — which is when the ladder runs. |
39	
40	## 4. Release material
41	
42	**`CHANGELOG.md`** gets a `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` section at the top, one theme per bullet, in the same words as the English half of the Release body. An `## [Unreleased]` section written by implementers is a completeness checklist, not draft prose: rewrite it into the release section, then **delete the whole `## [Unreleased]` section it came from**, leaving exactly one such section in the file — the empty one the next change writes into. A second `## [Unreleased]` left behind reads as a duplicate release, which is what happened at 0.2.3.
43	
44	**The GitHub Release body** ships both languages: Chinese first, English below, with a language switcher at the top and the sections 新增功能 / 体验优化 / 问题修复 / 其他变更 mirrored in English.
45	
46	- Open with one line naming the previous version; close with the install block, the compatibility line, and a Full Changelog compare link.
47	- Write the register of DeepSeek Harness's own release notes: about eight bullets of one sentence each, naming the theme rather than its sub-behaviours.
48	- Leave out metrics, internal nouns, and file names; state what the version *is*, not what changed about it.
49	- GitHub rewrites raw HTML anchor ids, so the switcher's jump has not worked since 0.1.7; the switcher line is still the required shape, pending a maintainer decision.
50	
51	**The pinned compatibility discussion** in `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` (discussion 4303) is a public surface with no sync path, which is why `check:public-baseline` exists. Maintenance is a rotation over three comments of our own: post the new release comment, fold the previous version into the version-history comment, then delete our own previous release comment by node id — post, verify, then delete. Never edit or delete anyone else's comment; the thread legitimately carries external comments and replies beyond our three.
52	
53	## 5. Publish
54	
55	Assert all four release-semantics facts **before** pushing or publishing:
56	
57	1. The tag is exactly `v<package.json version>` — no drift between manifest and tag.
58	2. A prerelease suffix matches the GitHub Release's prerelease flag; a stable release is not flagged prerelease.
59	3. Publishing names the dist-tag explicitly — `npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public`, with `<dist-tag>` `latest` for a stable version and the prerelease's own tag otherwise. npm refuses a prerelease published under the default tag, so an omitted `--tag` cannot express this release at all: the run stops there rather than moving `latest`.
60	4. A release that takes `latest` never moves it backwards: the current `latest` must be semver-lower than the version being published.
61	
62	```sh
63	git add package.json CHANGELOG.md
64	git commit -m "chore: release X.Y.Z"
65	git push --dry-run origin master            # fence: this must list exactly master
66	git push origin master
67	```
68	
69	Wait for this run to be green on both lanes (§2.6) before tagging:
70	
71	```sh
72	git tag vX.Y.Z
73	git push --dry-run origin vX.Y.Z            # fence: this must list exactly the tag
74	git push origin vX.Y.Z
75	npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public
76	```
77	
78	The explicit refspecs and their dry-run fences are load-bearing, not ceremony. A clone can carry pre-rewrite backup branches and local-only tags whose commits are deliberately absent from the remote, and `--all` / `--tags` publish them silently. This repository is public: a stray ref cannot be withdrawn. If a dry run lists a third ref, stop and find out whose it is.
79	
80	Pushing master before the tag costs nothing and keeps the tag's evidence honest: the run that certifies a tag is the run of the commit the tag names. A tag may be re-pointed only while nothing references it yet — no GitHub Release, no npm version, no consumer.
81	
82	## 6. Post-publish verification
83	
84	1. `npm view @contexera/dsh-agent-team dist-tags.<dist-tag>` — equals `X.Y.Z`, the tag §5 published under. A release that took `latest` also moves the packument's own `version`; a prerelease on its own tag leaves `latest` where it was.
85	2. The GitHub Release exists, carries an explicit title, and renders both language sections.
86	3. The pinned compatibility discussion shows the new release comment.
87	4. The stable profile installs the release by **exact version**: `dsh plugin --profile web add @contexera/dsh-agent-team@X.Y.Z`. A plain `update` can report "Already up to date" because the lockfile pins the resolution; the profile must not be left reading a newer ledger with an older bundle, since both profiles share `$DSH_HOME/storages/`.
88	5. A **fresh install in an empty directory** loads the bundle from the registry — not from the checkout, and not through a source symlink.
89	6. The prose corrected in §2 step 4 still says the right thing when read back from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, not just from the working tree.
90	7. `npm run check:public-baseline` is green against the published version.
91	
92	Registry reads lag right after a publish: the version document can be served before the full packument, so `npm view <name>` may briefly report the previous version, or `E404` for a package that is live. Never re-publish to "fix" a lag — poll the packument, or prove the artifact by installing from the tarball URL.
93	
94	## 7. Never
95	
96	- Never re-publish, unpublish, or move a tag that an existing release references. `npm deprecate` is the only sanctioned cleanup.
97	- Never rewrite shipped release material — the `CHANGELOG` entry, the Release body, or the release comment of a version that already published. Fix forward in the next patch. The single exception is a factual error found within minutes, corrected with maintainer approval.
98	- Never widen `peerDependencies` before certification has passed; a range claim is a support claim.
99	- Never publish from a tree with an uncommitted change to a build input.
100	- Never `git push --all` or `git push --tags`.
101	- Never `git add -A` in the shared worktree; stage your own paths.
