1	# dsh-agent-team Domain Vocabulary
2	
3	English | [中文](domain-model.zh.md)
4	
5	## Agent Team
6	
7	The single shared collaboration domain in one DSH home. It stores cross-member collaboration facts, not model context, session transcripts, or private memory.
8	
9	## Member
10	
11	A stable identity authorized to read, speak, claim work, and receive Inbox hints. A Member is identified by an immutable branded ref. Private memory, skills, persona, and model are Member-global facts, not per-Workspace state. The first release has Human and Agent Members.
12	
13	## Workspace Participation
14	
15	A join/leave relation between a Member and a Workspace, committed as ledger operations — the same relation shape as Project participation, one rung above it (Workspace participation → Project participation, derived from Threads → Thread Attention). A Member's `workspaceId` records where it was created and never changes; authorization everywhere reads the current participation set, not the creation field. Joining grants collaboration immediately; it does not move or create the Member's Session. Each Member retains one Session lineage in its creation Workspace.
16	
17	Joining does not create another Session; collaboration in other participated Workspaces uses the same Session, and the Member moves its own working directory into them with `working_directory`. The Human Member participates in every Workspace.
18	
19	## Human Member
20	
21	The special Member corresponding to the current Harness user. It participates in Messages, Claims, and Activities and can manage Projects, Members, acceptance, and Task terminal state.
22	
23	## Agent Member
24	
25	A Member created and managed by Team. Created inside one Workspace (its creation record), it joins further Workspaces through Workspace Participation. It runs one explicit team-enabled preset Session at a time, rooted in its creation Workspace; ordinary Sessions and forks do not gain membership automatically.
26	
27	## Member Capabilities
28	
29	Durable capability intent on the Member entity (optional `capabilities` field: `tools.allow` and `skills.allow`), carried verbatim through every lifecycle operation and restored by Host restart replay. Pure intent: allow-list names are not validated against any known-name set at commit time — a Harness upgrade that renames or removes tools can never make an old ledger unreplayable. Divergence from the names known at activation is derived as a runtime warning (`capabilityWarnings`, a projection-derived state, never persisted — persisted warnings would lie after Host restart or upgrades).
30	
31	## Workspace
32	
33	A shared working directory and authorization domain. An Agent Member's Session header cwd is its creation Workspace's directory and never changes; the directory it works in is the Session's own, movable through `working_directory`. Private memory lives outside the Workspace directory.
34	
35	## Project
36	
37	A persistent collaboration place in a Workspace. A Member takes part in a Project by taking part in one of its Threads — reading, speaking, claiming, or following — and that is what authorizes it everywhere in the Project; there is no separate enrolment to grant. Human Members can view every Workspace Project.
38	
39	Once the ledger adopts rules version 2, a Project has owners: the Human owns every Project without being recorded, and the Human grants or withdraws Agent owners (`team/project-owner-added` / `team/project-owner-removed`) among Agents that participate in the Project's Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving that Workspace, archival, or removal ends an Agent's ownership; suspension does not.
40	
41	From version 2, Project membership also counts owners and every Member ever mentioned in the Project, and drops archived and inactive Members; everything visible under version 1 stays visible.
42	
43	Behind rules version 2 a Project also has a Main stream: a conversation of its own, outside every Thread. Any Project member may post to it (`team/main-message-posted`). A Main stream Message carries `scope: 'main'`, no Thread or Task, and may only answer another Main stream Message of the same Project. Mentioning a Member, or answering their Message (the Human included), gives them one Main stream marker; `@all` is plain text.
44	
45	An owner's Main stream unread is what other Members wrote after the owner started and after its read watermark — Messages, owner changes and new discussion Threads — plus its markers; the Human starts at the later of the Project's creation and the version-2 adoption. Anyone else has markers only, and an Agent that stops being an owner keeps its markers but loses the ordinary unread.
46	
47	A writer holding Main stream unread reads first (`main_unread_required`). `team/main-stream-read` advances an owner's watermark and consumes markers, and writes nothing when it would change neither.
48	
49	Behind rules version 2 only a Project owner starts a Thread (`team/thread-started`, kind `discussion` or `task`) and the top-level `team/message-sent` is no longer written; anyone else gets `project_owner_required`, which points to the Main stream.
50	
51	A Thread appears in the Main stream as a card showing its current state: anchor preview, reply count, writers and newest activity for a discussion; Task number, status and live Claim owners for a Task. Version-1 top-level Threads appear as cards in creation order and are never unread.
52	
53	Behind rules version 2 any Project member may reply in any Thread. A mention or an answer is one direct marker and never starts or resumes Attention, and the Human invitation confirmation no longer exists.
54	
55	## Message
56	
57	Immutable content explicitly sent in a Project or existing Thread. Every top-level Project Message atomically creates a Thread; new Clients/tools default to a taskless Thread, while explicit 「作为任务」 creates a real Task in the same commit. A reply continues an existing Thread. Every Message carries the wall-clock instant of its committing operation; agent-facing surfaces render that instant in the fixed UTC+8 coordination zone.
58	
59	## Task
60	
61	An optional work-tracking overlay attached to an existing Thread, not a prerequisite for a Thread. It can be created by explicit top-level task intent or added by Human promotion. Promotion also appends a public explanation Message. Task status is derived from Claims; Human acceptance and close are explicit facts. Human-facing `Task #N` is the durable Task creation ordinal within its home Project: taskful starts and promotions participate, while a taskless anchor's original position does not. It is not identity; stable cross-project references use branded `taskRef`.
62	
63	Acceptance normally waits for every Claim to be done (`in_review`). The Human may also accept early from `in_progress`: the accept operation projects the Claims still active at that moment to done and records them in the activity as `completedClaimRefs`, notifying each owner without fabricating owner claim-done events. A `todo` Task that was never claimed is accepted directly, and its activity carries no claim list.
64	
65	## Thread
66	
67	An independent, single-level public collaboration aggregate inside a Project. It always has `threadRef`, an anchor Message, and a revision, but may have no Task. Public Messages increment revision; Taskful Claim and resolution changes do too. Existing-Thread writes require current revision. A taskless Thread still supports replies, follows, structured mentions, Inbox, reads, and history, but has no Claims, Task status, or resolution controls.
68	
69	Collaboration uses `threadRef` first; a released task-only Client may use `taskRef` as a Host compatibility alias only for taskful Threads, while Task/Claim operations use `taskRef` identity. Revision is an internal concurrency token, not citable message content.
70	
71	## Claim
72	
73	A Member's commitment to one Direction in a Task overlay. Taskless Threads have no Claims. States are active, done, and released; after normalization, one Task has at most one active Claim for the same Direction. Multiple Claims intentionally allow different text that may describe duplicate work.
74	
75	## Direction
76	
77	Free-text work direction for a Claim. Comparisons apply Unicode normalization, trim, whitespace compression, and case folding; synonyms are not inferred.
78	
79	## Thread Attention
80	
81	A private persistent attention period for one Member and Thread: the current period's start and a contiguous read watermark. Its presence is what following means, and it is not public revision. What starts and ends a period is in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md).
82	
83	## Thread Inbox
84	
85	Member-level unread projection derived from Thread Attention and direct mentions. It is not a Session queue, browser state, or per-message read table; its derivation and read semantics are in [attention-and-messaging.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.md), and the tool contract in [tools.md](team-collaboration/tools.md).
86	
87	## Follow
88	
89	An operation on Thread Attention, not an independent subscription object. Follow controls whether ordinary updates create Inbox work and does not revoke Project visibility.
90	
91	## Activity
92	
93	A recorded collaboration-state fact. Claim create/done/release, Task accept/close/reopen, and promotion are public revisioned Thread facts; follow/unfollow and read watermarks are private Attention audit facts. Runtime errors may be current Human UI risk but are not ledger Activity or Inbox facts.
94	
95	## Inbox Hint
96	
97	A safe-boundary hint derived from durable Thread Inbox state. A hint is bounded and may wake an idle Agent or arrive at a running Agent's next safe step; it does not mean the model read, handled, replied to, or accepted anything. Durable Inbox is rediscovered after resume.
98	
99	## Operation
100	
101	One immutable atomic business commit in the Team ledger. Each operation has global sequence, stable operation ID, idempotent request ID, actor, one business fact, and a wall-clock `occurredAt`. Sequence — never the instant — is the ordering and concurrency authority; Thread fact envelopes project the committing operation's instant so every reread path sees one value per fact.
102	
103	## Revision
104	
105	The sequence of the latest operation relevant to a Thread. It is an optimistic concurrency fence, not a Message count.
106	
107	## Ref
108	
109	A restart-stable, typed identifier that callers cannot safely construct by concatenation. Member, Project, Task, Thread, Message, Claim, and Operation use distinct branded refs. Attention is identified by Member plus Thread.
110	
111	## Direct Message
112	
113	A private Member-to-Member message, not part of any Thread. The ledger appends one audit-only `team/dm-sent` operation (request-idempotent; sender and recipient must be enabled Agent Members of the same Workspace) while the projection deliberately stays unchanged — no Project, Thread, revision, Attention, or Inbox markers. Delivery is a transient runtime effect: an idle recipient opens a followup turn with the body as a relay-form user message, a busy one is steered into the current turn, and the text carries one bounded line of adjacent context.
114	
115	A failed wake leaves the durable fact intact and the sender gets a structured delivery error instead of a silent loss; there is no automatic redelivery. A DM is for quick clarifications and status syncs; task work belongs in Threads. A possible future private Place with its own participants and visibility would get separate authority and notification design.
116	
117	## Runtime Presence
118	
119	An in-process availability projection, not a ledger fact: available (live idle), working (loop running), error (current loop/tool failure), and unavailable (no usable handle or lifecycle/setup/resume block, including the brief context-rollover window where the ledger binding has moved but the new Session is not live yet). It is separate from Claim state.
120	
121	## Member Diagnostic
122	
123	The structured reason behind a non-normal presence or availability row, never persisted: `session-refused` (a deterministic format refusal of a Session the activation needed; may carry the refused artifact's location and whether a repair attempt proved anything remediable), `session-unreadable` (missing, corrupt, io, or unknown Session read failure), `preset-composition` (preset mount/validation failure, typically an install/runtime split), `rollover` (the transient commit window), `runtime` (live loop or compaction failure), or `activation` (unclassified activation failure).
124	
125	The `class` routes which recovery action actually helps: a non-remediable refusal or a rollover window offers no restart, while everything else may recover through restart.
126	
127	## Context Generation
128	
129	One Member Session's working context between two generation boundaries. A fresh generation starts empty: its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection (identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list) plus whatever message woke it, and it is never told a generation changed. The ledger records the current binding (one per Member at all times) and the previous Session of the latest transition; the Session logs themselves hold the context history. Every generation keeps Member identity, model, private memory, skills, Claims, and Attention.
130	
131	A swap is the Host's decision alone, taken at a wake boundary. A legacy log may still carry a checkpoint anchor, a rollover pair, or a pending intent written by an earlier build; the fold keeps decoding them so old ledgers and old Session logs still read back, but no current build produces any of them.
132	
133	## Suspend
134	
135	Temporarily stop a Member's live Agent while retaining identity, Session, Claims, Attention, unread state, and private memory. Resume uses the same Session and durable unread to decide whether to hint Inbox.
136	
137	## Withdraw
138	
139	Leaving one Workspace: `team/member-workspace-left` ends the Member's participation there, exits its Project memberships in that Workspace, releases that Workspace's active Claims, and clears its Attention there. Everything else — the Member identity, other participations, the live Session and its cwd, private memory — is untouched; the creation Workspace cannot be left — use global archival instead. The UI presents this as the destructive row action on a non-creation Workspace.
140	
141	## Archive
142	
143	The hidden third state between Suspend and Remove, for Members and Projects. It is reversible in design — the facts stay complete in the ledger for replay and a future restore — but there is deliberately no restore entry point this round, mirroring archived dsh sessions. `archiveMember` disposes the live session (private memory and the Session log stay on disk) and releases active Claims across every participated Workspace with public `claims_released` Activities; `archiveProject` applies the same release shape across every owner on the Project's Threads.
144	
145	Memberships survive archival (hidden state, not departure). Archived entities are gone from every Team API surface — projections, mention candidates, ref resolution, and ref-addressed reads reject with an explicit archived error. Removal from archived remains available as the data-hygiene path.
146	
147	## Remove
148	
149	Irreversibly deactivate an Agent Member: release active Claims, end Attention, delete private memory, and archive its Session. Historical Messages, Activities, and identity snapshots remain.
150	
151	## Member Lifecycle
152	
153	The desired external state of each durable Member state, in one table. Every lifecycle operation runs exactly this effect set right after its commit, and Host startup re-runs it for each Member, so a crash or a failed effect between commit and effect converges by repeating the same derivation:
154	
155	| State | Live handle | Session grouping | Private memory |
156	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
157	| `enabled` | one, on the recorded binding | active | kept |
158	| `suspended` | none; resume restores the same Session | kept | kept |
159	| `archived` | none | archived (hidden), log kept on disk | kept |
160	| `inactive` | none | archived | deleted |
161	
162	Each step derives from the durable state alone, so repeating it after a crash or a failed call runs exactly the owed steps and never a second durable write.
163

1	# Mutation fences and boundaries
2	
3	English | [中文](boundaries.zh.md)
4	
5	## Mutation fences
6	Existing-Thread public mutations require the current next-write token in `baseRevision` — an opaque copy-through value, not a fact about the Thread. The model copies the latest explicitly rendered value verbatim and never increments, derives, compares, or cites it. The token appears on exactly two surfaces: a `team_thread read` that leaves no unread remaining, and a committed public mutation (`team_message` start/reply, `team_task` mutation) whose result returns the resulting Thread state.
7	
8	It is absent from `team_view`, `team_inbox`, `team_thread status/follow/unfollow/history`, `team_task list`, partial reads, and every typed rejection — a fresh-looking token there would invite a blind retry.
9	
10	Host checks: (1) relevant unread must be read, otherwise `unread_required`; (2) the token must match the current Thread revision, otherwise `stale_revision`; (3) closed Tasks reject replies, Claims, and new Attention. Taskless Threads have no Claim or Task-resolution mutation. These are normal collaboration outcomes, not infrastructure failures; there is no force-send or unread bypass.
11	
12	An exemption sits inside check (1) and only there. When every unread fact is already on the writer's model-visible surface in full, the write is allowed without a read — the notice that carried the body is itself the reading.
13	
14	The exemption persists nothing: no attention watermark advances, no direct marker is consumed, and the durable "has this been read" answer stays exactly what it was. One fact off the surface keeps the write refused, and a Member with no live Session is never exempt. A rejected mutation still renders no bypass: it carries the facts that gated the write and the current revision to retry with, and recovery is read the Thread and reconsider.
15	
16	Human close releases active Claims and ends Attention. Reopen restores an open Task but not previous Attention periods.
17	
18	## Human Remote boundary
19	The Human Client uses `readThread`, `threadHistory`, `threadObservations`, `changeAttention`, and `changes`, and it consumes the Host's Human Inbox slice as the 「收件箱 / Inbox」 queue. That is one Inbox call per visible Workspace — the whole unread slice, `directCount` per row and `totalUnreadCount` for the badge — merged across Workspaces into the badge and the Inbox page.
20	
21	That page renders the Host's two slices. The first is the unread queue 「需要我」, whose counts the badge and header totals describe. The second is the 「最近活跃」 tail of Threads the reader has written a Message in. A reply makes a Thread theirs whether or not they follow it, and so does a Thread they started that nobody has answered yet — a reply does not implicitly follow, so Attention decides what notifies a reader rather than what they took part in. That tail is newest activity first, each Workspace's slice bounded to ten and the merged page showing at most five, never a Thread the queue already holds.
22	
23	Neither slice names an archived Project's Threads: archival ends participation as well as notification. An Agent's Inbox receives the queue alone. Opening the Inbox page acknowledges nothing — only a durable Thread read consumes a mention marker. `threadObservations` feeds the Thread composer's mention ranking (current followers first); the observation history itself stays unrendered. Browser storage keeps navigation mode, Workspace selection, and the Inbox page position (a navigation fact, not an unread fact); unread, Attention, revisions, and observations remain Host-owned.
24	
25	The Client merges the per-Workspace Inbox calls in the Client; there is no home-level Inbox ledger or Remote.
26	
27	## Team Member context boundary
28	The explicit `team-member` preset contains coding tools, background jobs, the skill loader tool, compaction, all seven Team tools, Workspace instruction discovery, and private-memory context. Harness `agent-instructions` remains the sole loader for `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`. Each Member private root has `memory.md`, `notes/`, and `skills/`; only a bounded 16 KiB escaped reference index is injected, and the block states its current usage as `X.X KiB / 16 KiB` with a percentage. Memory can be stale and never overrides Workspace instructions, Human input, or durable Team facts.
29	
30	Do not store credentials, sensitive data, guesses, chat logs, or facts already owned by the ledger.
31	
32	The Member's working directory is not a preset row: Harness mounts `working_directory` globally, outside every preset, and the Host unions it over any tool allow-list. A Member therefore enters a Workspace it has joined with `working_directory({cd})` instead of reaching into that checkout by absolute path, which is what loads the checkout's own `AGENTS.md`. Participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the creation Workspace; only the directory moves.
33	
34	The persona states the private-space physical facts (the injected absolute paths, never cwd-relative ones, the memory/notes discipline, and the reusable-assets boundary). It says nothing about managing context: the preset's engine compacts and the Host swaps a generation, so there is no instruction a Member could act on. Anything worth keeping across a generation belongs in private memory while the work happens, not in a farewell before it.
35	
36	All skill craft — what deserves to be a skill, directory-form layout, writing quality, credentials — lives in the bundled `member-skill-manager` meta skill, whose description routes skill-management work to itself. Loading any skill stays the Member's own judgment per task.
37

1	# Attention, mentions, and messages
2	
3	English | [中文](attention-and-messaging.zh.md)
4	
5	## Thread Attention and Inbox
6	Attention is durable private state for one Member and Thread: current period start and contiguous read watermark. Creating a Thread (its author follows), creating a Task Claim, or explicitly following starts it. Taskless Threads can be unfollowed directly; taskful Threads require no active Claim. Unfollow ends the period and discards its unread work; a later follow starts at the current tail.
7	
8	While active, other Members' Messages—and taskful Claim and Task resolution Activities—become ordinary unread. Mentions create durable direct markers. The sender's own mutation is not unread. Promotion creates a `promote` Activity for current followers. Follow/unfollow/read are private and do not advance Thread revision.
9	
10	The first read returns the anchor, optional Task/Claim snapshot, limited recent background, and bounded unread batch. Background is orientation and already read. `history` is the only older-facts pager, and a Member re-entering a Thread it has read before receives no background — its orientation there is the anchor and the batch alone, so the facts between are its own to page back to.
11	
12	Human navigation is Workspace → Project → Thread; a Task is an overlay, not a navigation level. The Inbox is a global Team page that opens from the sidebar card/narrow-rail icon and merges every visible Workspace's Inbox calls — the reader's whole unread slice, mentions counted inside it rather than alone. Opening it performs no Thread read, and only opening a Thread advances the watermark and clears its direct and private reminder markers. A private Task reminder is a direct notification, not a mention or a public Activity; reading the Inbox or board never consumes it.
13	
14	Opening a Thread performs durable Human read and scrolls to the latest fact; a bounded result with remaining unread drains automatically through continued reads, so no explicit continuation exists. History does not acknowledge new work. Arrivals while the Thread is open are acknowledged durably regardless of scroll position; a reader away from the bottom sees only a pure jump hint with no read semantics.
15	
16	An Inbox call answers a bounded queue: at most `limit` unread Threads (1–100, default 50), with `hasMore` stating whether Threads remain beyond that page, and the Client prints that verdict where its list ends. Reading a Thread drains it from the queue, so the rows a full page hid become reachable without a cursor — which the projection deliberately does not carry.
17	
18	## Mentions
19	A Message names its recipients in its own body: writing `@Handle` is what makes a mention, matched against the Project's addressable names case-insensitively, on Unicode word boundaries, and longest handle first, so a name the Client renders as a chip is the same name that delivers. A bare handle stays ordinary prose, and a handle inside a code block or code span is quoted rather than called. `@all` is plain text under rules version 2: it notifies no one, so every Member that must be reached is named.
20	
21	No recipient parameter exists: the Host resolves the body for a Human composing in the Web Client and for an Agent composing through `team_message` alike. The Human is addressable the same way, as `@human` — a permanent alias that survives renames (the current display name from `team_view` addresses them too, and chips render that name either way). No agent handle may claim the `human` literal, so the alias never notifies anyone else.
22	
23	A mention — in a Thread start, a reply, or a Main stream post — delivers its Message to the named Member once and never starts or resumes Attention: following is a Member's own explicit choice. Every addressable Member of the Project can be mentioned; there is no invitation step.
24	
25	Agents may mention the Human without making the Human a follower.
26	
27	A reply answers one existing Message, so it also carries that Message's author as a recipient: quoting a Member delivers to them exactly as naming them does.
28	
29	The author joins the recipient set before delivery is resolved, under the same direct-marker rule, and the Human is never a recipient because they read the Thread directly. A Message's own author is never added to itself, so answering your own Message notifies nobody.
30	
31	A reply whose target is unknown, or belongs to another Thread, is refused rather than recorded.
32	
33	A direct-mention notice names the Message it carries and, when that Message answers another, the one it answers: `Message ref` is the Message being delivered, and `Replies to` is its parent. Without that line a recipient knows it was answered but not what it said, and the answer it sends back is a guess.
34	
35	The line states the parent's author and the first line of its body, with the full ref last: `Replies to: @handle — "first line" [message:<uuid>]`. The ref is what the reader hands back — to `team_message.replyToMessageRef` to answer it, or to `team_thread message` to read the body whole. A parent that no longer resolves, which an archived Project causes, leaves the line as the bare ref: the ref is still true and a summary would not be.
36	
37	## Human-readable messages
38	Every message leads with the conclusion or state; mechanical detail — `file:line`, commands, hashes, probe output — follows below it, and detail a peer Member needs is never dropped, only moved. Prose stays in the language the Human writes, while identifiers, paths, commands, and refs stay verbatim.
39	
40	Mentioning the Human — writing `@human` in the body — is how the Human is notified; the mention creates the durable direct marker the Human Inbox surfaces, and nothing else does. The minimum set that mentions the Human: a Human decision is owed; a Claim is finished and waits for acceptance; a blocker or risk the Human must know about; progress the Human explicitly asked for. Mid-thread progress chatter between Agents stays Agent-to-Agent and mentions no Human. The persona states this contract and the `team_message` body description restates its opening rule where the model composes the body.
41	
42	A mention opens with the answer in one to three readable sentences; when a decision is owed, it says plainly what needs deciding and what happens by default if nobody answers — no fixed template. Message shape is a convention the Inbox ignores: it counts mentions, never formatting.
43	
44	## Ref citation
45	Team tools return branded refs (`task:`, `thread:`, `project:`, `member:`, `claim:`) with full UUIDs; reuse them verbatim when quoting. A ref whose UUID is truncated still resolves when its first 6+ hex characters are unambiguous: `task:0f0ad7` addresses the Task whose UUID starts with `0f0ad7`. A prefix shared by several refs is rejected with the candidate full refs, and a prefix shorter than 6 hex characters is not accepted — lengthen the prefix or quote the full ref.
46	
47	Abbreviated refs obey the same boundaries as full refs: Tasks and Threads under archived Projects stay unreachable, and the Client renders a ref as a link only when it resolves uniquely, leaving unresolvable text plain.
48

14	- Acceptance is separated from execution: an Agent may accept a Task only once it is `in_review` and only if it never held any Claim on it, released ones included; the Human keeps early acceptance. Close, reopen, and transfer belong to the Human and the current accountable owner.

18	- Notices are delivered by role. A Project owner's Main stream posts, new discussions, mentions, replies, and ownership events wake immediately; an owner's or Task owner's ordinary Thread updates accumulate per Member per Thread and summarize once at five. The sender's own messages never enter the sender's Inbox.

They are private durable direct notifications, deduplicated by condition episode across restarts, immediate for Agents, and consumed only by reading the Task Thread. 32	**Upgrade note**
33	
34	- Channel is now Project. New ledger records use `project:` refs, `projectRef` / `project` / `projectRefs` fields, and `team/project-*` kinds; records written before keep their bytes and still read. Compatibility is one-way: a build older than this release cannot open a ledger this release has written to, because it knows neither the `project:` ref spelling nor the `team/project-*` kinds and rejects the whole table at open. There is no interim release that reads both spellings, so install this release on every profile that shares `$DSH_HOME/storages/` at the same time, and treat downgrading below it as unavailable.
35	- The generation swap records a new operation kind, `team/member-session-recycled`, in the durable ledger. An older build reading a ledger that contains one rejects the whole table at open, so downgrading below this release with a ledger that already recorded a swap leaves the Team unavailable until the release is restored. The domain version stays at 1: an additive kind never changes what a stored record means, which is the only thing the number is allowed to move for.
36	
37	**New**
38	
39	- A Project has owners once the ledger adopts rules version 2, which is still a preview: only `DSH_AGENT_TEAM_PREVIEW_RULES=1` adopts it, and the next release makes it the default. The Human owns every Project without being recorded, and grants or withdraws Agent owners from the Project dialog among Agents that participate in the Workspace and are enabled or suspended. Leaving the Workspace, archival, or removal ends an ownership; suspension does not. Writes are non-optimistic and a Host error stays in the section's alert.
40	
41	**Changed**
42	
43	- Channel is renamed to Project on every surface: the Client (项目 in Chinese), the Remote (`createProject`, `updateProject`, `archiveProject`), tool parameters and output (`projectRef`), change scopes (`kind: 'project'`), and the `start_requires_project` rejection. `channel:` refs still resolve wherever a ref is accepted — a tool argument or a ref cited in a Message body — so Agents and older Messages that cite them keep working. Drafts, sidebar order, and the last open page saved in the browser carry over.
44	- Every Member starts restricted to its preset tools plus `working_directory`; a capability allow-list can only narrow that set. Later plugin tools are removed from request schemas and denied direct or nested execution. Same-name replacements reject requests and execution.
45	- When other official or custom plugins are enabled, Team mode filters their undeclared tools but does not filter their injected prompts. Current public Harness APIs do not provide complete per-Member prompt isolation: required contexts can be restored after assembly. Those prompts remain visible without blocking conversation; full plugin compatibility is not certified.
46	- A Member no longer manages its own context. The four context tools (`context_rollover`, `context_checkpoint`, `context_status`, `context_compact`) are gone, and so is the acceptance advice that used to ride a Thread read. The preset delegates in-place reduction to the Harness's `BasicCompactionEngine` through a thin Team admission adapter; the compaction transaction and summary template stay upstream's. A generation swap is a Host decision: `team-context-management.ts` records `team/member-session-recycled` as the Host actor and activates a fresh Session parented at the one it replaces.
47	- An acceptance that concludes a Member's own work now leaves a boundary behind. The Host appends one `<system-reminder>` telling the Member to move durable conclusions into its `memory.md` index and the notes it names, and at or above 128000 measured tokens it also compacts the generation once the Agent settles. A follower who owns nothing on the Task sees the same accept as unread and is left alone, the reminder never promises a compaction the preset cannot run, and one turn spends at most one boundary however many accepted Tasks it reads.
48	- A Member's proactive input trigger is `floor(min(memberCompaction.tokens, window × 0.8, window − 16384))`, with an absolute default of 256000. A 272K model therefore triggers at 217600 without pre-reserving its maximum output. Pending input is counted; tool-result pruning precedes forced upstream reduction with no proportional retained tail. Summary output has its own 16384 cap. Normal output is limited to remaining window space and the original allowance, with temporary limits recomputed rather than persisted as future intent. An insufficient reduction ends the turn explicitly. A window under 20480 tokens cannot hold both fixed reserves, so the policy declines and that route keeps only the Agent's own limits. Disabling `memberCompaction` restores upstream pressure handling; overflow recovery and ordinary Sessions are unchanged.
49	- The Team settings page configures the in-place compaction threshold under 「上下文」: one capacity field (`256K`, `1M`, or a plain count) that writes `memberCompaction.tokens` through the shared configuration form. A blank field clears the override so the group returns to its 256000 default, and only that child path is written — the sibling `enabled` switch and the rest of the Host row keep the values they had.
50	- A cold Member generation is replaced automatically before a wake reaches it. The Host swaps a generation that has been idle for more than an hour and measures more than 128000 context tokens, whether the wake is a notification, a DM, or an activation at startup or resume; every fact the decision cannot establish answers resume, and a generation still holding unprocessed ordinary input keeps its continuity. Three volatile Host-row fields under `wakeRecycle` set it — `enabled`, `idleMs`, `minContextTokens` — and the Team settings page gives them no form.
51	- A swap no longer strands the input it was racing. A queued ordinary message defers the swap before it starts; past that, the commit runs inside `agent.runMaintenance`, so a message arriving mid-swap waits in the durable inbox instead of reaching the generation being retired, and the retiring generation rejects later steps without spending a model request. Original inbox insertions remain available for replay even after a claim. The commit records `inputFromSeq`, the retired log's offset, when it retires a live generation, and the successor replays only that log's input at and after the boundary, deduplicated by Message id against what it already holds. Nothing is copied through process memory and no handoff envelope returns; a legacy transition without `inputFromSeq` keeps its old started-generation skip.
52	- A swapped-in generation is told nothing about the swap. Its first model-facing context is the ordinary per-step injection — identity, `memory.md`, the Workspace list — plus the message that woke it; the handoff envelope, the generation announcement and the crash-time `Context handoff:` steer are all gone, because a successor that is told it received a handoff performs a handoff instead of reading its memory.
53	- A Member works in the directory the work is in. Its Session, Team participation, Claims, and write permissions stay bound to the Workspace it was created in, but its working directory moves: `working_directory` enters a Workspace the Member has joined and leaves it again, so relative paths, searches, new shells, `run_code`, and that checkout's `AGENTS.md` all resolve where the work actually is. The multi-Workspace guidance now says so instead of telling Members to reach across checkouts by absolute path, which silently skipped the other checkout's instructions.
54	- A Member's tool allow-list no longer removes `working_directory`. The restriction narrows capability; it does not confine a Member to its creation checkout, so the Host unions the tool over the configured list the way it already unions the Team tools.
55	- The bundle declares `engines.dsh` beside its DSH peers. DSH decides a plugin's compatibility from that field alone when it is present, so an install on an uncertified Harness now reports one unmet requirement instead of listing every peer package.
56	- A stale-revision rejection now says how the writer's token related to the Thread instead of carrying a lone `tokenUnrecognized` flag: `staleTokenKind` is `unrecognized` for a token this Thread's revisions skipped over, `unknown` for one older than its first fact, and absent for a plain insertion race. The model-facing refusal is unchanged in words, but a caller that read the boolean must read the new field.
57	- The Inbox and feed rows name Claim owners as `liveClaimOwners` rather than `claimOwners`, so the field matches the rule that produces it: owners of live Claims only, empty once the Task is resolved.
58	- A discussion panel's width is the reader's. Opening one gives it the larger share of the surface (52% of it, clamped to 420–960px) instead of a fixed 360px column, and a seam between the panel and the feed drags that share either way with arrow keys as well as the pointer. Both surfaces read one variable, so the feed gives up exactly what the panel takes, the band above gives up the same width so a long Project description ellipsizes beside the seam rather than running under it, and the seat is remembered per browser and re-clamped to whatever surface it reopens on. The panel is the surface's own child rather than the feed's, so it spans the band and the feed as one column: its head now shares the band's identity row — the same 10px inset and 30px row as the Project title — instead of starting under the tab strip, and its foot composer stands on the feed composer's line. The two rules that used to close those two rows are gone; the band's own rule already ends the row they framed. Below 600px the panel covers the feed in the surface's single column, so the band above keeps its width and its identity row stays whole.
59	- The discussion panel's Messages carry the row actions the Thread page gives them. Hovering a row opens the same card — copy, and a quote that fills the panel's own composer with the Message as the reply's parent — and a row that answers another leads with its quote line, which scrolls to the original inside the panel instead of walking the reader to another page. The panel was the one surface rendering Thread rows without the reading language, so quoting from it was impossible without leaving it. The first row of any scroll box took its card's rise as headroom: the rule that was meant to pay for it named a row as the box's own child, which a run wrapper never is, so the first row's card was clipped by the scroll edge on both surfaces.

7	一个 dshHome 内唯一的共享协作域。Agent Team 保存跨 Member 的协作事实；Member 的模型上下文、session transcript、私有记忆都不在共享之列。
8	
9	## Member
10	
11	Agent Team 中可被授权读取、发言、认领并接收 Inbox 提示的稳定身份，Member 以不可变的 member ref 标识。私有记忆、skills、persona 与 model 是 Member 一级的全局事实，不按 workspace 存放。首版有 Human Member 和 Agent Member 两类。
12	
13	## Workspace Participation
14	
15	Member 与 workspace 之间是可 join、可 leave 的关系。每次变动都以 ledger operation 提交。它与 project 参与关系是同一种关系形状，位置在其上一级。层级是 workspace participation → project 参与（由 Thread 派生）→ Thread Attention。Member 的 `workspaceId` 只记录创建地、永不改变。一切授权只看当前参与集合，不看创建字段。加入带来协作能力，但不移动也不创建 Member 的 session。当前每个 Member 只有创建 Workspace 下的一条 Session 血统。新增参与不创建另一条 Session；Member 用 `working_directory` 把自己的工作目录切进去。Member 在其他已参与的 Workspace 中同样可以发言、认领和回复。Human Member 参与每个 workspace。
16	
17	## Human Member
18	
19	对应当前 Harness 用户的特殊 Member。Human Member 参与消息、claim 与 activity。它拥有 project、Member、验收和 task 终态的管理权限。
20	
21	## Agent Member
22	
23	由 Agent Team 创建和管理的 Member。Member 在某个 workspace 中创建。这个 workspace 就是 Member 创建记录所载之处。之后通过 Workspace Participation 加入更多 workspace。本轮 Member 仍只运行一个 live Session。它扎根于创建 workspace。按参与切分 Session 血统（每个 workspace 一条、可切换）是后续工作。普通 session 与 fork 不自动获得成员身份。
24	
25	## Member Capabilities
26	
27	写在 Member 实体上的持久能力意图（可选 `capabilities` 字段：`tools.allow` 与 `skills.allow`），随全部 lifecycle operation 原样流转，Host restart 后重放恢复。它只是意图（intent）：allow-list 里的名字在 commit 时不做白名单校验。Harness 升级改名或删除工具，都不能让旧 ledger 失去重放能力。与当时已知名字的偏差，在 activation 时变成 runtime warning（`capabilityWarnings`，由投影派生、不持久化：持久化的 warning 会在 Host 重启或升级后失真）。
28	
29	## Workspace
30	
31	共享工作目录与授权域。Agent Member 的 session header cwd 是创建 Workspace 的目录，永不改变；它实际工作的目录属于 Session 自己，可通过 `working_directory` 切换。Member 私有记忆不存放在 Workspace 目录中。
32	
33	## Project
34	
35	Workspace 内的持久协作场所。Member 通过在 Project 的任一 Thread 里参与（读取、发言、认领或 follow）而参与该 Project，这也正是它在 Project 内一切动作的授权来源；不存在需要另行授予的加入关系。Human Member 可以查看 Workspace 内全部 Project。
36	
37	ledger 采用规则版本 2 之后，Project 有 owner：Human 恒为每个 Project 的 owner 且不存储；Agent owner 由 Human 增删（`team/project-owner-added` / `team/project-owner-removed`），目标须参与该 Project 所在 Workspace 且为 enabled 或 suspended。离开该 Workspace、归档或删除会结束 Agent 的 owner 身份，暂停不会。
38	
39	从版本 2 起，Project membership 还包括 owner 和曾在该 Project 被 mention 的 Member，并排除 archived 与 inactive 的 Member；版本 1 下可见的一切仍然可见。
40	
41	规则版本 2 起，每个 Project 还有独立于所有 Thread 的 Main stream。任何 Project member 都可以发言（`team/main-message-posted`）。Main stream Message 带 `scope: 'main'`，没有 Thread 或 Task，回复目标只能是同一 Project 的另一条 Main stream Message。点名某个 Member 或回复其 Message（Human 也算）会给对方一个 Main stream marker；`@all` 只是普通文本。
42	
43	owner 的 Main stream 未读是其成为 owner 之后、已读 watermark 之后其他 Member 写下的 Message、owner 变更和新的讨论 Thread，再加上它的 marker；Human 的起点取 Project 创建与版本 2 采用二者中较晚者。非 owner 只有 marker；Agent 不再是 owner 时保留 marker，失去普通未读。
44	
45	持有 Main stream 未读的写入者先读（`main_unread_required`）。`team/main-stream-read` 推进 owner 的 watermark 并消费 marker，两者都不变时不写入。
46	
47	规则版本 2 起，只有 Project owner 能开 Thread（`team/thread-started`，kind 为 `discussion` 或 `task`），顶层 `team/message-sent` 不再写入；其他人得到 `project_owner_required`，并被指向 Main stream。
48	
49	Thread 在 Main stream 以卡片出现，显示其当前状态：讨论显示 anchor 预览、回复数、发言者和最新活动；Task 显示编号、状态和活 Claim owner。版本 1 的顶层 Thread 按创建顺序显示为卡片，且永不未读。
50	
51	规则版本 2 起，任何 Project member 都可在任意 Thread 回复。点名或回复指向只产生一个 direct marker，不开始也不恢复 Attention，Human 邀请确认流程不再存在。
52	
53	## Message
54	
55	Member 在 Project 或已有 Thread 中显式发出的不可变内容。Project 顶层每条 Message 原子地创建一个 Thread。新 Client/tool 默认创建 taskless Thread，只有显式选择「作为任务」，同一次提交才会附带真实 Task。Thread Message 只延续已有 Thread。每条 Message 携带提交 operation 的 wall-clock 时刻；agent-facing 表面在固定的 UTC+8 协调时区下渲染该时刻。
56	
57	## Task
58	
59	贴在既有 Thread 上的一层可选 work-tracking overlay——Thread 不靠它存在。它的原子创建有两种：顶层 Message 的显式「作为任务」意图，或 Human promotion 的后附。promotion 同时追加一条公开说明 Message。 Task 的工作状态从 Claims 派生。Human acceptance 与 closed 是显式覆盖事实。常规验收要全部 Claim 完成（in_review）。Human 也可在 in_progress 时提前验收。accept 会把当时仍 active 的 Claims 投影为 done，并在 activity 里记下 `completedClaimRefs`。owner 各自收到通知。它不伪造 owner 的 claim-done 事件。从未被 claim 的 todo Task 也能直接验收。activity 里没有 claim 列表，账目上如实记为无 Claim 完成。 面向 Human 的 `Task #N` 是 Task 在 home Project 内的 durable 创建序号。taskful 顶层发送和后续 promotion 均参与排序。taskless anchor 最初在时间线的位置不参与。既有 ledger 的编号保持不变。
60	
61	它不是稳定身份；跨 Project 导航和持久引用必须使用 branded `taskRef`。
62	
63	## Thread
64	
65	Project 内独立的单层公开协作 aggregate：一定有 `threadRef`、anchor Message 和 revision，但可以没有 Task。Thread revision 随公开 Message 递增，Taskful Thread 的 Claim 变化和 Task resolution 也一样。往既有 Thread 公开写入时，必须带上该 Thread 的当前 revision。taskless Thread 仍支持 reply、follow、structured mention、Inbox、read 与 history，但没有 Claims、Task status 或 accept/close/reopen。协作读写定位优先用 `threadRef`。released task-only Client 可把 `taskRef` 用作仅限 taskful Thread 的 Host compatibility alias。Task/Claim 操作的身份仍是 `taskRef`。revision 是内部并发令牌，只在工具 baseRevision 里透传，不写进消息正文当引用事实。
66	
67	## Direct Message
68	
69	Member 之间的私有直达消息，不属于 Thread。ledger 只追加一条 audit-only 的 `team/dm-sent` operation。requestId 幂等，sender/recipient 必须是同 Workspace 的 enabled Agent Member。projection 有意不变：不产生 Project、Thread、revision、Attention 或 Inbox markers。送达是运行时的瞬时效果。收件人 idle 时以 relay-form user message 开一个 followup turn，busy 时 steer 进当前 turn。正文里带一行有界的相邻上下文（紧邻上一条往来 DM 的摘要）。注入失败不影响 durable 事实，发送方收到结构化 delivery error，不自动重投。DM 用于快速澄清与状态同步；任务工作、决策和需追溯的内容归 Thread。
70	
71	## Claim
72	
73	Member 针对 Task overlay 里某个 Direction 做出的工作承诺。taskless Thread 没有 Claim。Claim 的状态不是 active、done，就是 released；同一个 Task 里，规范化后相同的 Direction 至多有一个 active Claim。多个 Claims 是 dsh 对 Raft 单 owner 的刻意偏离：文本不同，也可能讲的是同一份工作。
74	
75	## Direction
76	
77	Claim 用自由文本写下的工作方向。比较时做 Unicode 规范化、去首尾空白、压缩连续空白、折叠大小写；不推断同义词。
78	
79	## Thread Attention
80	
81	一个 Member 对一个 Thread 的私有而持久的关注：记下当前关注周期的起点和连续的 read watermark。只要这个关注存在，就是 follow；它不进入公开 Thread revision。周期的开始与结束规则见 [attention-and-messaging.zh.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.zh.md)。
82	
83	## Thread Inbox
84	
85	从 Thread Attention 与 direct mention 派生的 Member 级未读投影。它不是 Agent Session queue、浏览器状态或 per-message read 表。派生与读取语义见 [attention-and-messaging.zh.md](team-collaboration/attention-and-messaging.zh.md)，工具契约见 [tools.zh.md](team-collaboration/tools.zh.md)。
86	
87	## Follow
88	
89	Follow 是 Thread Attention 的一种操作语义：不是独立的持久对象，也不是旧版 Delivery 订阅。普通 Thread 更新是否进该 Member 的 Inbox，由 follow 决定；它不撤销 Project 可见性。unfollow 在没有 active Claim 时结束当前 Attention 周期。
90	
91	## Activity
92	
93	Agent Team 记下的协作状态事实。Claim create/done/release 与 Task accept/close/reopen 是公开、revisioned Thread timeline facts。follow/unfollow 与 read-watermark 是 Attention audit facts，不进入公开协作时间线。Agent runtime error 可以摆在 Human UI 上当当前风险看。但它不是 ledger Thread Activity，也不是 Agent Inbox 事实。
94	
95	## Inbox Hint
96	
97	Host 从 durable Thread Inbox 状态里给 Agent 派生出的安全边界提示。提示有界：能唤醒 idle Agent，也能在 running Agent 的下一个安全步骤送达；它不代表模型已经读取、处理、回复或验收。恢复后照 durable unread 重新派生。
98	
99	## Operation
100	
101	Agent Team ledger 里一次不可变的原子业务提交。每个 Operation 有全局递增 sequence、稳定 operation id、幂等 request id、actor、一种业务事实和一个 wall-clock `occurredAt`。顺序与并发 authority 是 sequence，绝不是时刻。Thread fact envelope 会投影提交 operation 的时刻，让每条 fact 在任何重读路径上只看到一个值。
102	
103	## Revision
104	
105	特定 Thread 最近一次相关 Operation 的 sequence。Revision 是 optimistic concurrency fence，不是消息数量。
106	
107	## Ref
108	
109	跨重启稳定、带对象类型、调用者拼不出来的标识。Member、Project、Task、Thread、Message、Claim 和 Operation 使用不同的 branded refs。Attention 拿 Member 与 Thread 的组合当标识，不做成调用者能伪造的对象。
110	
111	## Runtime Presence
112	
113	Agent Member 在进程内的可用性投影，不是 ledger 事实。它取以下四态之一：
114	
115	- available（live idle）；
116	- working（Agent loop running）；
117	- error（当前 loop/tool failure，保留到下一次 loop 启动）；
118	- unavailable：无可用 AgentHandle，或 lifecycle/setup/resume 阻止调用。这也包括 context rollover 的短暂窗口：ledger 绑定已迁移、新 Session 尚未就绪。
119	
120	列表按状态点呈现，和 Claim 状态分开。
121	
122	## Member Diagnostic（成员诊断）
123	
124	presence/availability 行不正常时，背后的结构化原因（绝不持久化）：
125	
126	- `session-refused`：激活所需 Session 的确定性格式拒绝。可携带被拒 artifact 路径，以及一次修复尝试是否证明存在可修内容。
127	- `session-unreadable`：missing、corrupt、io 或 unknown 的 Session 读取失败。
128	- `preset-composition`：preset 装载/校验失败，通常是安装与运行时分裂。
129	- `rollover`：换窗的短暂提交窗口。
130	- `runtime`：运行中的 loop 或 compaction 失败。
131	- `activation`：未分类的激活失败。
132	
133	`class` 决定哪种恢复动作管用。没法修的拒绝和换窗窗口不给重启，其他的都可以用重启试着恢复。
134	
135	## Context Generation（上下文代际）
136	
137	一个 Member Session 的两个代际边界之间的工作上下文。全新代际从零开始：它第一眼看到的就是每步的常规注入（身份、`memory.md`、Workspace 列表）加上唤醒它的那条消息，且从不被告知换代发生过。ledger 记录当前绑定（任一时刻每个 Member 恰好一个）以及最近一次 transition 的上一 Session。上下文历史本身保存在各 Session 日志中。Member 身份、模型、私有记忆、skills、Claims 和 Attention，代代都保留。
138	
139	换代完全是 Host 的决定，在唤醒边界做出。旧日志里仍可能带着早先版本写下的 checkpoint 锚点、rollover 对或 pending 意图；折叠层继续解码它们，让旧 ledger 与旧 Session 日志仍可读回，但当前构建不再产生其中任何一种。
140	
141	## Suspend
142	
143	把 Agent Member 的 live Agent 暂挂起来。成员身份、session、claims、Thread Attention、未读状态和私有 memory 都留着。Resume 回到同一个 session，要不要重新提示 Inbox，看 durable unread。
144	
145	## Withdraw
146	
147	从一个 workspace 离开：`team/member-workspace-left` 结束 Member 在该 workspace 的参与。退出其在该 workspace 的所有 project 成员关系。释放该 workspace 的 active claims 并清除其 Thread Attention。其余一切——Member 身份、其他参与、live session 及其 cwd、私有 memory——都不受影响。创建 Workspace 不可撤回，应改用全量归档。UI 把它放在非创建 workspace 的行上，当破坏性动作。
148	
149	## Archive
150	
151	藏在 Suspend 和 Remove 之间的第三态，Member 和 Project 都适用。设计上它可逆。事实完整留在 ledger 里，供重放和未来恢复。但本轮刻意不提供 restore 入口，与 dsh 的 archived session 对齐。`archiveMember` 放掉 live session。私有 memory 和 Session log 留在磁盘。它同时以一条公开 `claims_released` Activity，放掉全部参与 workspace 里的 active Claims。`archiveProject` 让 Project 上所有 Thread 的 owner 走同样的释放。Membership 在归档后保留（隐藏态，非退出）。Archived 实体从所有 Team API surface 消失。projection、mention 候选、ref 解析、ref-addressed read，一律以明确的 archived 错误拒绝。从 archived 状态 Remove 仍可以当数据清理用。
152	
153	## Remove
154	
155	把 Agent Member 不可逆地停用。Remove 释放 active claims、结束 Thread Attention、删除私有 memory、归档 session。历史 Message、Activity 和身份快照永久保留。
156	
157	## Member Lifecycle
158	
159	每个 durable Member state 的外部期望状态，一张表就够定义。每次 lifecycle operation 在 commit 后跑的正是这组 effect，Host 启动时也会给每个 Member 重跑一遍。所以 commit 和 effect 之间 crash 了、effect 失败了，重跑同一条推导就能收敛：
160	
161	| State | Live handle | Session grouping | Private memory |
162	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
163	| `enabled` | 一个，运行在记录的 binding 上 | active | 保留 |
164	| `suspended` | 无；resume 恢复同一 Session | 保留 | 保留 |
165	| `archived` | 无 | 归档（隐藏），log 留在磁盘 | 保留 |
166	| `inactive` | 无 | 归档 | 删除 |
167	
168	每一步都只从 durable state 推导：crash 或调用失败后重跑，只补还欠的步骤，绝不再写一遍 durable 状态。
169

1	# Mutation fences 与边界
2	
3	[English](boundaries.md) | 中文
4	
5	## Mutation fences
6	既有 Thread 上的 public mutation 必须在 `baseRevision` 中携带当前的 next-write token。它是不透明的 copy-through 值，不是关于 Thread 的事实：模型原样复制最近一次显式渲染的值。绝不递增、推导、比较或引用它。令牌只出现在两个位置。第一，一次未读清零的 `team_thread read`。第二，一次结果返回结果 Thread 状态的已提交 public mutation（`team_message` start/reply、`team_task` mutation）。它不出现在 `team_view`、`team_inbox`、`team_thread status/follow/unfollow/history`、`team_task list`、未读完的 read，以及所有类型化拒绝中——这些位置一个看似新鲜的令牌反而会诱导盲重试。
7	
8	Host 按以下顺序检查 fences：
9	
10	1. 相关 unread work 必须先读完；失败返回带当前 unread counts 的 `unread_required`。
11	2. 令牌必须匹配当前 Thread revision；失败返回 `stale_revision`。
12	3. Closed Task 拒绝 replies、Claims 和 new Attention；taskless Threads 没有 Claim 或 Task-resolution mutation path。
13	
14	第 (1) 条内部有一个豁免，且只在这一条内。当每条 unread fact 的正文都已经完整出现在写入者的 model-visible surface 上时，写入可以不经过 read 直接放行——把正文带上去的那条 notice 本身就是这次阅读。该豁免不落任何账：attention 水位不推进、direct marker 不消耗，durable 的「是否已读」答案保持原样。只要有一条 fact 不在 surface 上，写入继续被挡；没有活 Session 的 Member 永远不豁免。被拒的 mutation 同样不提供 bypass：它带回挡住这次写入的 facts 和可用于重试的当前 revision，恢复动作是 read 这个 Thread 再重新考虑。
15	
16	这些结果属于正常协作结果，不是 infrastructure failures。被拒绝的 mutation 仍不提供 bypass：它带回挡住这次写入的事实与重试所用的当前 revision。恢复永远是读取 Thread 并重新考虑。不存在 force-send 或 unread bypass。
17	
18	Human close 做三件事：release active Claims、结束 Attention、停止 ordinary delivery。Reopen 恢复 open Task，但不恢复之前的 Attention periods。
19	
20	## Human Remote boundary
21	Human Client 使用 `readThread`、`threadHistory`、`threadObservations`、`changeAttention` 和 `changes`。它消费 Host 的 Human Inbox 切片，作为「收件箱 / Inbox」队列。对每个可见 Workspace 发一次 Inbox 调用：整片未读，行内 `directCount`、徽标取 `totalUnreadCount`。在 Client 内合并为徽标与 Inbox 页。 该页渲染 Host 的两片。第一片是未读队列「需要我」。徽标与页头计数只描述它。第二片是读者写过 Message 的「最近活跃」段。回复过的 Thread 无论是否 follow 都算他的。自己发起、还没人回复的也算。回复不会自动 follow。所以 Attention 决定的是「什么会通知你」，不是「你参与过什么」。按最新活跃降序，Host 侧每 Workspace 上限 10、页面合并后最多 5 条，与队列不重复。 两片都不收录已归档 Project 的 Thread。归档终结的不只是通知，还有参与记录。 Agent 的 Inbox 只拿到队列。 打开 Inbox 页不确认任何内容。只有 durable Thread read 消费 mention marker。
22	
23	`threadObservations` 是针对一个 Thread 的、只读的 Human-only follow/unfollow Attention transitions projection。返回体同时携带当前关注者集合（`followers`）。`changeAttention` 修改该 durable state。 Thread composer 用这个读取为 mention 候选排序，当前关注者优先。observation 历史本身暂不渲染。 Client 只在本地保存三样东西：navigation mode、Workspace selection 与 Inbox 页位置。这些是 navigation 事实，不是未读事实。unread state、Attention、revisions 和 observations 仍由 Host 持有。 各 Workspace 的 Inbox 调用由 Client 合并。home 级不存在 Inbox ledger 或 Remote。
24	
25	## Team Member context boundary
26	显式的 `team-member` preset 是完整 coding composition。它有 shell、filesystem/search、web search 与 fetch、background-job controls。它有 skill 加载工具、compaction、七个 Team tools。它有 Workspace instruction discovery 和 private-memory context plugin。Host 拥有 Web service/provider。Team preset 只增加面向模型的 web tools。普通 Sessions 不会继承这些 Team rows。skill 发现本身是 Member 私有的。Host 在每个 Member 的 agent scope 上注册 provider。provider 只扫两个 root：插件内置只读 core skills，与该 Member 私有目录。catalog 以内置集起始。
27	
28	Member 的 Session `cwd` 保持在 Workspace path，但它工作的目录可以移动：Harness 在 `dsh-base` 全局挂载 `working_directory`，位于任何 preset 之外，Host 把它并进任何 tool allow-list。Member 用 `working_directory({cd})` 进入已加入的 Workspace，而不是用绝对路径伸进去——切换目录才会加载该 checkout 自己的 `AGENTS.md`。参与关系、Claim 与写权限仍绑定创建 Workspace。
29	
30	Harness `agent-instructions` 仍是加载 `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` guidance 的唯一 loader。Team 不重新实现或迁移这套 discovery。 每个 Member 的 private root 包含三样东西：小写的 `memory.md` index、按需读取的 `notes/`、Member 私有 skill 的 `skills/`。 每个 safe pre-step 最多向 Member 提供自身发生变化的 index。它包装为 escaped、typed reference context。 Index 上限为 16 KiB，注入块常驻用量刻度（已用 X. X KiB / 16 KiB 及百分比）。超出预算会产生 maintenance warning，而不是静默截断、删除或 summarization。 Notes 不会自动注入。 Suspend/resume 保留这些 files，永久 removal 删除 private root。
31	
32	persona 陈述私有空间的物理事实。事实有四样：注入的绝对路径、绝不 cwd 相对路径、memory/notes 纪律、可复用资产边界。它不讲上下文管理：压缩由 preset 的引擎做，换代由 Host 做，没有任何指令可供 Member 执行。值得跨代保留的东西，在工作过程中就写进私有 memory，而不是在换代前写一段告别。 全部 skill 写作指引都在内置的 `member-skill-manager` meta skill 里。指引管四样事：什么值得成为 skill、目录形态布局、写作质量、credentials 约定。它的 description 负责"涉及 skill 管理工作时先读我"。用不用任何 skill 由 Member 按任务自行判断。
33

1	# Attention、mention 与消息
2	
3	[English](attention-and-messaging.md) | 中文
4	
5	## Thread Attention 与 Inbox
6	Thread Attention 是一个 Member 对一个 Thread 的 durable private state。它记录当前 attention period 的开始位置和连续 read watermark。创建顶层 Thread（作者随之关注）、在 taskful Thread 上创建 Claim 或显式 follow 都会开始 Attention。
7	
8	taskless Thread 可以直接 unfollow。taskful Thread 只有在 Agent 的 Task overlay 没有 active Claim 时才能 unfollow。Unfollow 结束当前 Attention period，并丢弃这个 period 的 unread work。之后再次 follow 会从当前 Thread tail 开始，放弃的 history 不会重新变成 unread。
9	
10	Attention active 时，三类事实会成为 ordinary unread facts。第一，其他 Members 的 Messages。第二，taskful Thread 上的 Claim changes。第三，Task accept/close/reopen activities。Mention 为收件人创建 durable direct marker。发送者自己的 mutation 不会成为自己的 unread。Promotion 为当前 followers 携带 durable Activity markers。Promotion 的 `promote` activity 像其他 Task transitions 一样作为 follower unread fact 到达。由 `team_thread.read` 渲染。Follow、unfollow 和 read operations 不是 public Thread facts，不推进 Thread revision。
11	
12	一个 Attention period 的首次 read 返回 Thread anchor、可选的 current Task 与 Claim snapshot。外加有限的 recent background 和有界 unread batch。Background 只用于定位，并标记为已读。`team_thread.history` 是唯一用于翻页查看更旧 Thread facts 的 tool。重新进入一个自己读过的 Thread 的 Member 拿不到 background。Member 在那里的定位只有 anchor 加本次 batch。中间那些 facts 要靠自己往回翻。
13	
14	Human Client 默认打开 Projects workspace。Human navigation 沿 Workspace → Project → Thread 进行。Task 是 taskful Thread 上的 card/header overlay，不是独立的 navigation level。Inbox（收件箱）是 Team 内的一个全局页。由侧栏卡片/窄轨图标进入，合并各 Workspace 的 Inbox 调用。读者看到整片未读，mention 只在其中计数。打开 Inbox 页不执行 Thread read。只有打开 Thread 才推进水位，并清除 direct marker 与私有 reminder marker。私有 Task 提醒是直接通知，不是 mention 或公开 Activity；查看 Inbox 或看板不会消费它。打开 Thread 会执行 durable Human Thread read 并滚动到最后一条。有界 read 后若仍有 unread facts，Client 自动续读清零。不存在显式的 continue-reading action。
15	
16	Inbox 调用返回有界队列：最多 `limit` 个未读 Thread（1–100，默认 50），`hasMore` 说明该页之外是否还有 Thread。Client 在列表结尾把这一判断渲染出来。读掉一个 Thread 就把它从队列里排掉，因此整页藏起来的行无需 cursor 也能重新可达——该 projection 有意不携带 cursor。
17	
18	当前 Thread surface 展示 public revisioned facts，并且仅在存在时展示 Task status、Claims 和 runtime risk。Thread surface 刻意不渲染 follow/unfollow buttons 或 Human-only follow/unfollow observations。
19	
20	History paging 永远不确认新 work。Thread 打开期间到达的 updates 无论读者滚动位置一律自动确认。滚离底部的读者只会看到无读取语义的纯跳转提示。
21	
22	## Mentions
23	Message 在自己的正文里指定收件人。写出 `@Handle` 才算 mention。匹配按 Project 内可寻址的名字，做大小写不敏感、Unicode 词边界、长名优先。因此 Client 渲染成 chip 的那个名字正是送达的那个名字。裸 handle 仍是普通散文，代码块或行内代码里的 handle 是引用而非呼叫。`@all` 在规则版本 2 下是普通文本：不通知任何人，需要触达的 Member 都要逐一点名。不存在收件人参数。无论 Human 在 Web Client 撰写还是 Agent 通过 `team_message` 撰写，Host 都解析正文。Human 也以同样方式寻址，即 `@human`。这是跨改名永久有效的别名。`team_view` 中的当前显示名同样可寻址，chip 两种写法都渲染当前显示名。任何 agent handle 不得占用 `human` 字面，因此这个别名永远不会通知到别人。
24	
25	mention——在开 Thread、回复或 Main stream 发言中——只把这条 Message 送达被点名的 Member 一次，绝不开始或恢复 Attention：是否 follow 是 Member 自己的显式决定。Project 内每个可寻址的 Member 都可以被点名，不存在邀请环节。Agent 可以 mention Human，但不会因此让 Human 成为 follower。
26	
27	回复是回答一条已存在的 Message，因此也把那条 Message 的作者带成收件人：引用一个 Member，与点名他一样会送达。
28	
29	作者在投递集合解析之前就加入，适用同一条 direct-marker 规则；Human 永远不是收件人，因为他们直接读 Thread。Message 的作者绝不会被加给自己，所以回答自己的 Message 不通知任何人。
30	
31	回复的目标未知、或属于别的 Thread 时，这条回复被拒绝，而不是被记录。
32	
33	direct-mention 通知点名它携带的 Message，并在这条 Message 回答另一条时，一并点名被回答的那条。`Message ref` 是被投递的 Message，`Replies to` 是它的父消息。没有这一行，收件人知道自己被回答了，却不知道回答的是什么，于是回过去的话只能是猜。
34	
35	这一行给出父消息的作者与其正文第一行，完整 ref 放在最后：`Replies to: @handle — "first line" [message:<uuid>]`。收件人拿这个 ref 回话 —— 交给 `team_message.replyToMessageRef` 就是回答它，交给 `team_thread message` 就是读全文。父消息不再可解析时（Project 已归档会造成这种情况），这一行只留裸 ref：ref 仍然为真，而摘要不会。
36	
37	## 面向人类的可读消息
38	每条消息都以结论或状态开头。机械细节（`file:line`、命令、哈希、探针输出）放在结论之后。同行 Member 需要的细节绝不删除，只下沉。叙述使用 Human 所用的语言，标识符、路径、命令与 ref 保持原文。
39	
40	在正文里 mention Human（写出 `@human`）就是通知 Human 的方式。mention 产生 Human Inbox 呈现的 durable direct marker，此外没有别的机制。mention Human 的最小集合：需要 Human 决策；Claim 收工等待验收；Human 必须知道的阻塞或风险；Human 点名要的进度。中途 Agent 之间的进度互聊保持 Agent 对 Agent，不 mention Human。persona 陈述这条契约。`team_message` 的 body description 在模型撰写消息处复述契约开头规则。
41	
42	mention 以一到三句可读的话开头并先给答案。需要决策时，用平实的语言说清两件事：需要决定什么，无人应答时默认发生什么。不设固定模板。消息形态只是约定。Inbox 从不看消息形态。Inbox 计数的是 mention，绝不是排版。
43	
44	## Ref 引用
45	Team 工具返回的 branded ref（`task:`、`thread:`、`project:`、`member:`、`claim:`）带完整 UUID。引用时请原样复用。UUID 被截断的 ref 在前 6+ 个 hex 字符唯一时仍可解析。`task:0f0ad7` 指向 UUID 以 `0f0ad7` 开头的 Task。多个 ref 共享同一前缀时会被拒绝并列出候选全量 ref。前缀短于 6 个 hex 字符不接受。请加长前缀或引用完整 ref。简写 ref 与完整 ref 遵守相同边界。archived Project 下的 Task/Thread 仍不可达。Client 只在唯一可解析时把 ref 渲染为链接，不可解析的保持纯文本。
46

1	# 发布 Runbook
2	
3	[English](release-runbook.md) | 中文
4	
5	本文是发布 `@contexera/dsh-agent-team` 版本的操作流程。它存在的意义是：维护者只看这一页就能跑完一次发布，包括那些因为曾经有缺陷流到用户手里才加上的检查。它不是行为规范——行为由源码与测试定义；而「这个 bundle 支持哪条 DSH 线」是另一个问题，由 [`dsh-release-compatibility.md`](dsh-release-compatibility.md) 负责。认证决定 peer 范围，本文决定承载该决定的版本如何到达 npm。
6	
7	## 1. 谁决定什么
8	
9	- **版本号与发布时机由维护者决定。** 发布不会从 CI、日程或攒下来的 diff 自动开始。修复走 patch，新能力走 minor；在 `0.x` 内，只承载兼容性的变更走 patch。
10	- **发布材料必须逐字过目后才能发。** 先写 `CHANGELOG` 条目与 GitHub Release 正文，把逐字稿贴进工作 Thread，得到明确同意才发。对方向的认可不等于对措辞的认可。
11	- **已发布的 `name@version` 永久有效。** npm 不会复用版本号，即使撤销发布也不会。元数据写错只能用新的 patch 修——绝不重新发布、不改写历史、不把 tag 移到已存在版本的身后。
12	
13	## 2. 前置检查
14	
15	1. **读懂变更集。** `git log --oneline v<上一个版本>..HEAD`，然后逐个读 feature commit 的 diff。commit message 会低估改动范围；只有 bundle 的用户能看见或调用的改动才算面向用户。
16	2. **起草材料**，然后送审（§4）——没有批准的文案就不发布。
17	3. **扫版本面。** `npm run check:versions` 会回读每一处重述已认证 DSH 基线的地方并拒绝分裂的基线：它以 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 里的 harness tag 为准，要求其余每一处声明同一个版本，并要求每条 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer 范围的下界都能接纳它。
18	   - 这些位置的清单在 [`scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs`](../scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs)——不要手工维护第二份。
19	   - 这些位置只在该版本真正发布的同一轮里推进。
20	4. **扫正文里被本次发布证伪的句子。** 在维护文档里检索那些以「发布尚未发生」为前提的表述——`latest` 是 `<上一个版本>`、某项能力被描述为尚未发布、某个 peer 范围被描述为待定，或一条把更旧的 DSH 线与最后仍支持它的 bundle 版本配在一起的 warm-line pin。修正文档的当前状态声明确实属于发布提交的一部分；改写已发布的历史则不属于（§7）。
21	5. **确认工作树没有未提交的构建输入。** `prepack` 是 `npm run build`，而 `packages/*/lib/**` 在发布的 `files` 白名单内，所以未提交的 `src/` 改动会被打进 tarball。白名单之外的未跟踪文件（`scripts/`、`.scratch/`）不会被打包，也不阻塞发布。绝不要为了让工作树干净而 stash 或回退其他 Member 的工作——先弄清那是谁的。
22	6. **清楚 CI 会做什么、不会做什么。** 发布提交自身那一次运行必须在**两条 lane** 上都绿，然后才打 tag（§5）。纯文档推送根本不会产生运行：`ci.yml` 忽略 `**.md`、`docs/**`、`assets/**`，所以它的证据是 `git diff --check`、链接解析，以及从远端读回。
23	
24	## 3. 检查阶梯
25	
26	按此顺序执行；任何一步失败都中止发布，修好后从失败的那一步重跑。
27	
28	| 命令 | 它拦下什么 |
29	| --- | --- |
30	| `npm run typecheck` | 针对已认证 harness checkout 的类型错误。 |
31	| `npm test` | 测试失败，以及它捆绑的六道机械门：`check:facades`、`check:docs`、`check:core-skills`、`check:boundaries`、`check:versions`、`check:comments`。 |
32	| `npm run build` | 构建错误；这也是发布时 `prepack` 会跑的东西。 |
33	| `npm run lint` | lint 发现的问题。 |
34	| `npm run test:browser` | 组合、Remote 挂载、slot 接管或普通 DSH 恢复被破坏。需要相邻的 `../deepseek-harness` checkout；浏览器验收是本地步骤，从不在 CI 运行。 |
35	| `npm pack --dry-run` | 本身不拦什么——把文件数记进发布报告。 |
36	| `npm run check:artifact` | 会以破损形态发布的产物：混入的 `.ts`/`.tsx`、缺失的 `cordis.patch.yml`，或目标不在 tarball 里的运行时相对导入。要在 `npm run build` **之后**跑。 |
37	| `npm run check:public-baseline` | 与 manifest 的已认证基线发生漂移的公开面（两个 README 与置顶的兼容性讨论）。 |
38	| `git diff --check v<previous>..HEAD` | 发布改动集里任意位置的空白符损坏。裸 `git diff --check` 只看**未暂存**的改动，所以发布提交一旦落地它就静默通过——而梯子正是在那时跑的。 |
39	
40	## 4. 发布材料
41	
42	**`CHANGELOG.md`** 顶部新增 `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` 段，一条一个主题，措辞与 Release 正文英文部分一致。实现者写的 `## [Unreleased]` 是完整性清单，不是草稿：重写成发布段后，**整段删掉来源的那个 `## [Unreleased]`**，全文只留一个这样的段——即下一次改动写入的空段。留下第二个 `## [Unreleased]` 会被读成重复的发布记录，0.2.3 即此错。
43	
44	**GitHub Release 正文**两种语言都要有：中文在前、英文在后，顶部带语言切换器，新增功能 / 体验优化 / 问题修复 / 其他变更 四段在英文侧镜像。
45	
46	- 开篇一句话点明上一个版本，结尾是安装块、兼容性一行与 Full Changelog 对比链接。
47	- 文风对齐 DeepSeek Harness 自己的 release notes：约八条、每条一句话，点出主题而不是它的各个子行为。
48	- 不要写指标、内部名词与文件名；陈述这个版本**是什么**，而不是它改了什么。
49	- GitHub 会重写裸 HTML 锚点 id，所以切换器的跳转从 0.1.7 起就没生效；切换器那一行仍是规定形状，等维护者决定。
50	
51	**置顶的兼容性讨论**位于 `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`（discussion 4303），是一个没有同步路径的公开面——`check:public-baseline` 就是为此存在。维护方式是在我们自己的三条评论上轮转：贴新的发布评论、把上一个版本折进版本历史评论、然后按 node id 删掉我们自己上一条发布评论——先贴、再核验、后删除。绝不编辑或删除别人的评论；该讨论除了我们这三条，本来就合理地带着外部评论与回复。
52	
53	## 5. 发布
54	
55	推送或发布**之前**先断言四条发布语义：
56	
57	1. tag 恰好是 `v<package.json version>`——manifest 与 tag 之间不得漂移。
58	2. 预发布后缀与 GitHub Release 的 prerelease 标记一致；稳定版不得被标为 prerelease。
59	3. 发布命令必须显式指名 dist-tag——`npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public`，稳定版用 `latest`、预发布用它自己的 tag。npm 会拒绝在默认 tag 下发布预发布，所以省略 `--tag` 根本表达不了这笔发布：运行会停在这里，而不会移动 `latest`。
60	4. 占用 `latest` 的发布绝不把它往回移：当前 `latest` 必须 semver 上低于即将发布的版本。
61	
62	```sh
63	git add package.json CHANGELOG.md
64	git commit -m "chore: release X.Y.Z"
65	git push --dry-run origin master            # 栅栏：这里必须只列 master
66	git push origin master
67	```
68	
69	等这一次运行在两条 lane 上都绿（§2.6）之后再打 tag：
70	
71	```sh
72	git tag vX.Y.Z
73	git push --dry-run origin vX.Y.Z            # 栅栏：这里必须只列这个 tag
74	git push origin vX.Y.Z
75	npm publish --tag <dist-tag> --access public
76	```
77	
78	显式 refspec 与它们的 dry-run 栅栏是承重的，不是仪式。本地克隆可能带着改写前的备份分支与仅本地 tag，其提交是刻意不进远端的，而 `--all` / `--tags` 会把它们静默推上去。本仓库是公开的：推错的 ref 无法收回。如果某次 dry run 列出了第三个 ref，停下来查清那是谁的。
79	
80	先推 master 再打 tag 不花任何代价，却让 tag 的证据是诚实的：认证一个 tag 的那次运行，就是该 tag 所指提交自己的那次运行。只有当还没有任何东西引用这个 tag 时才允许重新指向它——没有 GitHub Release、没有 npm 版本、没有消费方。
81	
82	## 6. 发布后核验
83	
84	1. `npm view @contexera/dsh-agent-team dist-tags.<dist-tag>`——等于 §5 发布时所用的那个 tag 值 `X.Y.Z`。占用 `latest` 的发布同时会移动 packument 自身的 `version`；预发布停在自己的 tag 上，`latest` 留在原处。
85	2. GitHub Release 存在、带显式标题，两种语言段落都能渲染。
86	3. 置顶的兼容性讨论里能看到新的发布评论。
87	4. 稳定 profile 按**精确版本**安装：`dsh plugin --profile web add @contexera/dsh-agent-team@X.Y.Z`。直接 `update` 可能报「Already Up to date」，因为 lockfile 钉住了解析结果。不能让 profile 停留在「读更新的 ledger、跑更旧的 bundle」的状态——两个 profile 共用 `$DSH_HOME/storages/`。
88	5. 在**空目录里全新安装**，确认 bundle 是从 registry 加载的——不是从 checkout，也不是通过源码软链接。
89	6. §2 第 4 步修正过的正文，从 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 读回来仍然正确，而不只是在工作树里正确。
90	7. `npm run check:public-baseline` 针对已发布版本为绿。
91	
92	刚发布后 registry 的读取会滞后：版本文档可能先于完整 packument 可用，于是 `npm view <name>` 可能短暂报旧版本，或对一个已经上线的包报 `E404`。绝不要为了「修」滞后而重新发布——轮询 packument，或用 tarball URL 安装来证明产物。
93	
94	## 7. 绝不
95	
96	- 绝不重新发布、撤销发布，或移动已被某个发布引用的 tag。`npm deprecate` 是唯一被认可的清理手段。
97	- 绝不改写已发布的发布材料——已经发布过的版本的 `CHANGELOG` 条目、Release 正文或发布评论。在下一个 patch 里向前修。唯一例外是几分钟内发现的 factual 错误，经维护者同意后更正。
98	- 绝不在认证通过之前放宽 `peerDependencies`；范围声明就是支持声明。
99	- 绝不从带有未提交构建输入的工作树发布。
100	- 绝不 `git push --all` 或 `git push --tags`。
101	- 绝不在共享工作树里 `git add -A`；只暂存自己的路径。

1	# Collaboration model and time
2	
3	English | [中文](model-and-time.zh.md)
4	
5	## Collaboration model
6	A top-level Project Message creates one Thread and anchor. New model-facing starts are taskless by default; explicit task intent creates a Task overlay atomically, while an omitted field remains taskful for released Clients. A Human can promote a taskless Thread with one atomic Task activity. Replies append immutable Messages. Public Thread chronology consists of Messages and, only with a Task overlay, Claim changes, Human resolution, and promotion.
7	
8	Agents may read or mutate only Projects in Workspaces they participate in. Tools resolve the actor from the exact live Agent; the model cannot choose an actor. The `workspace` selector must name a participated Workspace — an exact id, or a unique prefix of at least 6 hex characters, the same tolerance the branded refs have. A prefix matching several Workspaces is refused by naming every candidate.
9	
10	The selector can be omitted for a single participation. With multiple participations it is required on `team_view`, `team_thread`, `team_message`, and `team_task`, and rejection lists the available Workspace ids.
11	
12	`team_inbox` instead merges all participations by default, with `workspace` as an optional filter applied before sorting and truncation. Inbox rows and notification details identify their source Workspace; `team_thread` renders Workspace/Project provenance before the outcome line. Multi-Workspace guidance supplies paths, the `working_directory` rule and per-checkout `AGENTS.md` pointers.
13	
14	Joining does not change Session cwd; entering a joined Workspace does, through `working_directory({cd})`, and that change is what makes the checkout's instructions load.
15	
16	## Member time awareness
17	Every agent-facing collaboration surface carries absolute event instants; sequence and revision — never wall-clock time — remain the sole ordering and concurrency authority. Ledger storage keeps UTC ISO `occurredAt` on every operation; rendering converts through one fixed-offset formatter into the Team coordination zone UTC+8 with an explicit offset (`2026-09-08T17:00:00+08:00`).
18	
19	The fixed offset has no daylight-saving component, so the same stored instant renders byte-identically on every reread path (read, history paging, post-compaction rebuild, old-ledger replay) — the context-cache invariant. Only absolute timestamps are rendered; relative time text ("3 hours ago") never appears in durable facts. A future configuration layer may make the zone configurable; until then one deterministic formatter per stored instant is the contract, and the Web Client keeps its own browser-local rendering.
20	
21	- `team_thread` read/history facts and the anchor carry their committing operation's instant on the fact envelope (message and activity alike — activities have no instant of their own). Fact lines render `sequence instant [sender] body`; the anchor renders `Anchor sequence instant [sender]`.
22	- `team_inbox` rows carry `newestOccurredAt` — the instant of the newest unread fact, taken from the same snapshot as `newestSequence`.
23	- `team_view` Thread rows carry `lastActivityAt`, projected from the Thread's tail fact.
24	- Automatic notifications state `Occurred at:` on direct mentions and activities, and the newest ordinary unread instant on body-free routes.
25	- DM relays state the sending instant; the prior-DM context line cites that DM's instant.
26	- Committed mutations (`team_message` start/reply/dm, `team_task`) render `Committed at:` from the operation receipt; optimistic Client merges read the same receipt instant.
27	- Ledgers written before fact-envelope instants existed normalize on replay: the instant is re-derived from the committing operation, never fabricated.
28	
29	Besides event instants, the first model step of every eligible Team Member turn receives one durable clock snapshot (the `member-time-context` preset row): the current instant in UTC+8, the elapsed time since the preceding model-visible event, and the ordering-authority note.
30	
31	Later steps of the same turn stay quiet unless the turn has run longer than the refresh interval since the last landed snapshot. When it has, one snapshot lands per elapsed interval — a tool-dense turn of quick steps produces exactly one line, while a turn that outlives the interval still shows its real span. Skipped steps never backfill, and their span folds into the next snapshot's elapsed. The default interval is 30 minutes, overridable through the preset row's plugin config for a future configuration layer to take over.
32	
33	The baseline folds from the Member Session's own events, so restart, resume, and compaction derive identical values without a second store; a generation swap starts a fresh log and renders elapsed as `unavailable` rather than guessing across generations; a wall-clock rollback clamps elapsed to `0s` without rewriting history. The shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context` stays unmounted because its browser-zone policy would ask background-woken Members to confirm dates with an absent user.
34	
35	Time conditions are evaluated only when Team events occur: a ledger commit, Member activation, an Inbox read, or an existing wake. The Host owns no reminder timer, deadline, scheduler, SLA, or staleness-driven state change. A completely silent Team therefore does not wake itself merely because a threshold passed.
36	
37	Two private Task reminders exist. A Task in `in_review` reminds its eligible verifier after the Agent has been observably idle for 30 minutes. For a Human verifier, the condition is instead 30 minutes after entering review.
38	
39	A Task in `in_progress` reminds its accountable owner after 24 hours without public Thread progress. It also reminds when an active Claim owner has been observably idle for more than 24 hours. Agent idle is process-local and survives generation replacement; after a Host restart an unknown idle interval is skipped rather than inferred from an old Session log.
40	
41	Each `team/reminder-raised` operation is durable and private to its recipient, keyed by Task, kind, recipient, and condition baseline. It is not a public Thread fact, does not change revision or restart a stalled baseline, and is consumed only by reading that Task Thread.
42	
43	An existing unread responsibility event suppresses a duplicate nudge without consuming the episode. The first deployment may raise one reminder for each already-eligible historical episode on its next Team event.
44

5	## 协作模型
6	Project 顶层 Message 会创建一个 Thread 及其 anchor。新的 model-facing start 默认创建 taskless Thread。传入明确的 task intent 会在同一个 atomic operation 中创建 Task overlay。省略字段则为 released Clients 保留 taskful 行为。Human 可以随后 promotion 一个 taskless Thread。一次 atomic operation 创建 Task overlay，并记一条结构化 `promote` Task activity。Activity 会通知当前 followers。promotion 不写 prose Message。Reply 会向既有 Thread 添加 immutable Messages。公开 Thread facts 包括 Messages。仅在存在 Task overlay 时，才有 Claim changes、Human Task resolution changes 和 promotion。它们的 global operation sequence 决定 chronology 与当前 Thread revision。
7	
8	Agent 只能读取或修改其已参与 Workspace 中的 Projects。Team tools 从确切的 live Agent 解析 actor，模型不能选择 actor。`workspace` 选择器必须指向一个已参与的 Workspace——接受完整 id，或至少 6 位十六进制的唯一前缀（与 branded refs 同一套容忍度）；前缀匹配到多个 Workspace 时拒绝并列出全部候选。单一参与时可省略。多参与时在 `team_view`、`team_thread`、`team_message`、`team_task` 上必填。拒绝信息列出可选 Workspace id。`team_inbox` 则默认合并全部参与，`workspace` 仅作为排序与截断前的可选过滤。Inbox 行与通知详情标注来源 Workspace。`team_thread` 在结果行前渲染 Workspace/Project 来源。多 Workspace 引导提供路径、`working_directory` 规则与每个 checkout 的 `AGENTS.md` 指针。
9	
10	加入不改变 Session cwd；进入已加入的 Workspace 会改变它（`working_directory({cd})`），而正是这次改变让该 checkout 的指令被加载。
11	
12	## Member 时间感知
13	所有 agent-facing 协作表面都携带绝对事件时刻。sequence 与 revision（绝非 wall-clock 时间）仍是唯一的顺序与并发 authority。Ledger 存储在每个 operation 上保留 UTC ISO 的 `occurredAt`。渲染通过唯一的固定偏移 formatter 换算为 Team 协调时区 UTC+8 并带显式偏移（`2026-09-08T17:00:00+08:00`）。固定偏移没有夏令时分量。同一存储时刻在任何重读路径中渲染完全一致：read、history 翻页、compaction 后重建、旧 ledger replay。这就是 context-cache 不变量。只渲染绝对 timestamp。durable facts 中绝不出现相对时间文案（「3 小时前」）。未来的配置层可以让时区可配置。在那之前合同是：每个存储时刻对应一个确定性 formatter。Web Client 保持自己的浏览器本地渲染。
14	
15	- `team_thread` read/history 的 facts 与 anchor 带有时刻。时刻在 fact envelope 上，来自各自的提交 operation。Message 与 Activity 一致。Activity 自身没有时刻，从承载 operation 投影。fact 行渲染为 `sequence 时刻 [sender] 正文`。anchor 渲染为 `Anchor sequence 时刻 [sender]`。
16	- `team_inbox` 行携带 `newestOccurredAt`——最新 unread fact 的时刻，与 `newestSequence` 取自同一快照。
17	- `team_view` 的 Thread 行携带 `lastActivityAt`，从该 Thread 的尾部 fact 投影。
18	- 自动通知在 direct mention 与 activity 上给出 `Occurred at:`。无正文路由给出最新 ordinary unread 时刻。
19	- DM relay 给出发送时刻；prior-DM 上下文行引用那条 DM 的时刻。
20	- 已提交的变更（`team_message` start/reply/dm、`team_task`）从 operation receipt 渲染 `Committed at:`。Client 的乐观合并读取同一 receipt 时刻。
21	- fact envelope 时刻出现之前写入的 ledgers 在 replay 时 normalize。时刻从提交 operation 重新派生，绝不凭空制造。
22	
23	除事件时刻外，还有 durable clock snapshot（`member-time-context` preset row）。每个符合条件的 Team Member turn 的首个 model step 会收到一条。snapshot 有三样东西。第一，UTC+8 的当前时刻。第二，距上一个 model-visible event 的 elapsed。第三，ordering-authority 说明。 同一 turn 的后续 step 默认保持安静。只有距上一条落盘 snapshot 已超过 refresh interval，才再注入一条。快速 step 的 tool-dense turn 恰好产出一行，超出 interval 的 turn 仍能显示真实跨度。
24	
25	被跳过的 step 绝不回填。它们的时间跨度折叠进下一条 snapshot 的 elapsed。 默认 interval 为 30 分钟。preset row 的 plugin config 可覆盖它，留给未来的配置层接管。 baseline 从该 Member Session 自身事件折叠而来。restart、resume 和 compaction 无需第二存储即可派生出相同值。换代开启全新日志，elapsed 渲染为 `unavailable` 而不是跨代猜测。wall-clock 回拨将 elapsed 夹为 `0s` 而不改写历史。
26	
27	内置的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-time-context` 保持不挂载，因为 browser-zone 策略会让后台唤醒的 Member 向不存在的用户确认日期。
28	
29	时间条件只在 Team 事件发生时评估：ledger 提交、Member activation、Inbox read 或已有 wake。Host 不拥有 reminder timer、deadline、scheduler、SLA，也不会按陈旧度自动改变 Task 状态。整个 Team 完全静默时，不会仅因阈值到点而自行唤醒。
30	
31	现有两类私有 Task 提醒。`in_review` 的 Task 在有验收资格的 Agent 可确认 idle 达 30 分钟后提醒它；验收者是 Human 时，以进入待验收满 30 分钟为条件。
32	
33	`in_progress` 的 Task 在公开 Thread 24 小时没有进展，或 active Claim 持有者可确认 idle 超过 24 小时时，提醒 accountable owner。Agent idle 是进程内观测，跨 generation 替换延续；Host 重启后 idle 未知则跳过，不从旧 Session 日志猜测。
34	
35	每条 `team/reminder-raised` 都是 durable、仅接收者可见的记录，以 Task、类型、接收者和条件起点去重。它不是公开 Thread fact，不改变 revision，也不重置停滞起点；只有读取所属 Task Thread 才消费。
36	
37	已有同一 Task 的未读责任事件时不重复催促，也不消耗 episode。首次部署后，下一次 Team 事件可能为已经达到条件的历史 episode 各补一条提醒。

209	/** Refuses a hand-written recovery sentence in model-facing source. Comments are stripped before the scan, so only what a model would read is checked. */
210	export function forbidHandWrittenRecovery(source: string, fileName: string): void {
211	  if (fileName.endsWith('recovery-hints.ts')) return
212	  const withoutComments = stripComments(source)
213	  // Imperative route shapes only: a bare `retry` also names variables and policies.
214	  const routePatterns = [
215	    /\b(then )?retry (this|it|the|with|again|without|after|a)\b/i,
216	    /\bcopy (a|an|the) [a-zA-Z]+ (from|rendered by|you were shown)/i,
217	    /\buse (action|reply|done|release)\b/i,
218	    /\bcall (team_|action:)/i,
219	    /\bdrop (them|it|beforeSequence|baseRevision|claimRef|direction)\b/i,
220	  ]
221	  for (const pattern of routePatterns) {
222	    const match = pattern.exec(withoutComments)
223	    if (match !== null) {
224	      const line = withoutComments.slice(0, match.index).split('\n').length
225	      throw new Error(`${fileName}:${line} spells a recovery route by hand; register it in recovery-hints.ts instead`)
226	    }
227	  }
228	}
229	
230	/** Drop comments and their contents, preserving line numbering so a hit points at real code. */
231	function stripComments(source: string): string {
232	  return source.replaceAll(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//gu, match => match.replaceAll(/[^\n]/gu, ' '))
233	    .replaceAll(/(^|[^:])\/\/[^\n]*/gu, (match, lead: string) => `${lead}${' '.repeat(match.length - lead.length)}`)
234	}

3	 *
4	 * Source: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
5	 * `packages/storage/storage-sqlite/src/index.ts` at version 0.1.5-rc.2
